#!/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14/bin/python3.14 import tkinter as tk from tkinter import messagebox, filedialog import random import json import os import sys from datetime import datetime # Module-level current theme name — _MacBtn is a standalone class (not # nested in App) so it can't read self.theme_name directly; this global # is kept in sync by App whenever the theme is set/switched. _CURRENT_THEME = "navy" class _MacBtn(tk.Label): """Drop-in replacement for tk.Button. On macOS, tk.Button ignores custom bg/fg colors — the native Aqua theme renders every button white/grey regardless of what's passed in. tk.Label respects colors correctly, so this class wraps a Label to behave like a Button (supports command=, hover via activebackground/activeforeground, and .config() the same way).""" def __init__(self, master=None, command=None, **kwargs): activebackground = kwargs.pop("activebackground", None) activeforeground = kwargs.pop("activeforeground", None) kwargs.pop("overrelief", None) kwargs.setdefault("cursor", "hand2") kwargs.setdefault("relief", "flat") # Real colored background with auto-contrast text — the previous # version forced every button to a fixed near-white background # regardless of the intended color or active theme; this uses # the actual intended color and picks readable text for it. # Exception: Retro theme deliberately recreates that original # accidental look on purpose, so it skips this and stays white. bg_in = kwargs.get("bg", kwargs.get("background")) if bg_in is not None: if _CURRENT_THEME == "classic": fg_in = bg_in kwargs["fg"] = fg_in kwargs["bg"] = "#eef0f4" bg_in = "#eef0f4" else: fg_in = _contrast_text_color(bg_in) kwargs["fg"] = fg_in kwargs["bg"] = bg_in if activebackground is None: activebackground = _lighten_color(bg_in) if activeforeground is None: activeforeground = fg_in base_bg = kwargs.get("bg", kwargs.get("background")) base_fg = kwargs.get("fg", kwargs.get("foreground")) super().__init__(master, **kwargs) self._command = command self._base_bg = base_bg self._base_fg = base_fg self._active_bg = activebackground self._active_fg = activeforeground self.bind("", self._on_click) if activebackground or activeforeground: self.bind("", self._on_enter) self.bind("", self._on_leave) def _on_click(self, event=None): if self._command: self._command() def _on_enter(self, event=None): cfg = {} if self._active_bg: cfg["bg"] = self._active_bg if self._active_fg: cfg["fg"] = self._active_fg if cfg: super().config(**cfg) def _on_leave(self, event=None): cfg = {} if self._base_bg: cfg["bg"] = self._base_bg if self._base_fg: cfg["fg"] = self._base_fg if cfg: super().config(**cfg) def config(self, **kwargs): cmd = kwargs.pop("command", None) kwargs.pop("activebackground", None) kwargs.pop("activeforeground", None) if cmd is not None: self._command = cmd # Same real-color-with-contrast remap as __init__ — keeps # toggled active/inactive states consistent if "bg" in kwargs: fg_for_bg = _contrast_text_color(kwargs["bg"]) kwargs["fg"] = fg_for_bg self._active_bg = _lighten_color(kwargs["bg"]) self._active_fg = fg_for_bg if "bg" in kwargs: self._base_bg = kwargs["bg"] if "fg" in kwargs: self._base_fg = kwargs["fg"] return super().config(**kwargs) configure = config def _contrast_text_color(hex_color): """Pick black or white text based on background luminance, so any colored button background stays readable. Module-level so both _MacBtn and App._btn can share the same logic.""" try: h = str(hex_color).lstrip('#') if len(h) != 6: return "#0a0a0a" r, g, b = int(h[0:2],16), int(h[2:4],16), int(h[4:6],16) luminance = (0.299*r + 0.587*g + 0.114*b) / 255 return "#0a0a0a" if luminance > 0.55 else "#f5f5f5" except Exception: return "#0a0a0a" def _lighten_color(hex_color, amount=0.18): """Lighten a hex color for a hover-state feel.""" try: h = str(hex_color).lstrip('#') if len(h) != 6: return hex_color r, g, bl = int(h[0:2],16), int(h[2:4],16), int(h[4:6],16) r, g, bl = [min(255, int(c + (255-c)*amount)) for c in (r, g, bl)] return f"#{r:02x}{g:02x}{bl:02x}" except Exception: return hex_color # Auto-installeer librosa als het niet aanwezig is def _check_librosa(): try: import librosa except ImportError: import subprocess subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "librosa", "numpy", "scipy", "--quiet"]) try: _check_librosa() except Exception: pass # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # 🎵 MUSICIAN'S CREATIVE SUITE v7.0 # Titels · Lyrics · Hook · Rap · Punchlines · Rijmen # BPM · Akkoorden · Song Structuur · Rijmzoeker # NL + EN · Favorieten · Geschiedenis # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # Data opslaan in ~/Documents/MCS zodat .app er altijd bij kan _MCS_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "Documents", "MCS") os.makedirs(_MCS_DIR, exist_ok=True) DATA_FILE = os.path.join(_MCS_DIR, "mcs_data.json") VERSION = "v7.0" # ── VERTALINGEN ────────────────────────────────────────── def t(nl_text, lang): """Vertaal NL naar EN op basis van taalinstelling.""" conns=CONNECTORS_NL if lang=="nl" else CONNECTORS_EN; suffs=SUFFIXES_NL if lang=="nl" else SUFFIXES_EN out=[] for _ in range(n): if genre: stijl=GENRE_STYLES[genre]; tmpl=random.choice(GENRE_FORMATS) p,s=random.choice(stijl["prefix"]),random.choice(stijl["suffix"]) else: tmpl=random.choice(formats); p,s="",random.choice(suffs) w1,w2=random.choice(words),random.choice(words); conn=random.choice(conns) out.append(tmpl.format(w1=w1,w2=w2,conn=conn,suf=s,p=p,s=s).strip()) return out def gen_lyrics_section(mood, lang, sectie): words=MOOD_WORDS[lang][mood]; suffs=SUFFIXES_NL if tmpl.format(w1=random.choice(words).lower(),w2=random.choice(words).lower(),suf=random.choice(suffs).lower()) def gen_rap_bars(mood, lang, schema="AABB", n=8): """Genereer rap bars met echte rijmende rijmdetectie — kijkt naar klank niet spelling. """ word = word.lower().strip() if not word: return [] # ── Fonetische normalisatie ─────────────────────────── def normalize_nl(w): """Zet Nederlandse spelling om naar klanken.""" w = w.lower() # Lange klinkers w = w.replace("ij","aj").replace("ei","aj") w = w.replace("ou","aw").replace("au","aw") w = w.replace("ui","oew") w = w.replace("oe","oo") w = w.replace("eu","uu") # Medeklinkers w = w.replace("ch","g").replace("sch","sg") w = w.replace("ng","nk") w = w.replace("ck","k").replace("kk","k") w = w.replace("dt","t").replace("td","t") w = w.replace("ff","f").replace("ss","s") w = w.replace("ll","l").replace("nn","n") # Stille letters aan einde if w.endswith("en"): w = w[:-2] + "e" if w.endswith("d"): w = w[:-1] + "t" return w def normalize_en(w): """Simplificeer Engelse spelling naar klanken.""" w = w.lower() w = w.replace("tion","shun").replace("sion","shun") w = w.replace("ight","ajt").replace("igh","aj") w = w.replace("ough","uf").replace("ought","awt") w = w.replace("ph","f").replace("ck","k") w = w.replace("kn","n").replace("wr","r") w = w.replace("mb","m").replace("gn","n") w = w.replace("gh","").replace("wh","w") w = w.replace("ee","ii").replace("ea","ii") w = w.replace("oa","oo").replace("ow","oo") w = w.replace("ou","aw").replace("oo","uu") # Cruciale fixes voor korte klinkers w = w.replace("ove","uv") # love/above/dove → luv/abuv/duv w = w.replace("ome","um") # come/some → cum/sum w = w.replace("one","un") # done/none → dun/nun w = w.replace("ong","ung") # song/long → sung/lung return w normalize = normalize_nl if lang == "nl" else normalize_en def get_rhyme_key(w): """ Haal het rijm-gedeelte op — klinker + alles erna. 'pijn' → 'ajn', 'nacht' → 'agt', 'flow' → 'loo' """ n = normalize(w) # Zoek laatste klinkergroep vowels = "aeiouáéíóúàèìòùäëïöüy" last_vowel_idx = -1 for i, c in enumerate(n): if c in vowels: last_vowel_idx = i if last_vowel_idx == -1: return n[-3:] # geen klinker gevonden — gebruik laatste 3 return n[last_vowel_idx:] # ── Grote rijmwoordenbank ───────────────────────────── NL_WORDS = """ ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ class App(tk.Tk): def __init__(self): # ── Fix for packaged .app builds: GUI apps launched via Finder/Dock # don't inherit the Terminal shell's PATH, so tools installed via # Homebrew (like ffmpeg) can be invisible even though the same code # works fine when run as `python3 script.py` from Terminal. Explicitly # add the common Homebrew bin directories if they exist and aren't # already on PATH — harmless no-op if ffmpeg is already found normally. for _brew_bin in ("/opt/homebrew/bin", "/usr/local/bin"): if os.path.isdir(_brew_bin) and _brew_bin not in os.environ.get("PATH", ""): os.environ["PATH"] = _brew_bin + os.pathsep + os.environ.get("PATH", "") # ── Theme (Classic / Navy) — load saved preference first, ── # before anything is built, so the whole app starts in the # right theme from the very first frame (including splash) global BG, BG2, BG3, BG4, BG5, BORDER, GOLD, GOLD_LT, FG, FG2, FG3, _CURRENT_THEME self.theme_name = "midnight" self.starfield_tabs = True try: if os.path.exists(DATA_FILE): with open(DATA_FILE, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f: saved = json.load(f) self.theme_name = saved.get("theme", "midnight") self.starfield_tabs = saved.get("starfield_tabs", True) except Exception: self.theme_name = "midnight" self.starfield_tabs = True _CURRENT_THEME = self.theme_name # MCS MEMORY — shared, session-only state so tools that assign # a role/priority to a track (Priority, Fit) don't need other # tools (Engine, Focus) to re-figure that out. Keyed by # filename (not full path, since the same file may be opened # from different dialogs across tools). self.mcs_memory = {} palette = THEME_PALETTES.get(self.theme_name, THEME_PALETTES["midnight"]) BG, BG2, BG3, BG4, BG5, BORDER = (palette["BG"], palette["BG2"], palette["BG3"], palette["BG4"], palette["BG5"], palette["BORDER"]) GOLD, GOLD_LT = palette["GOLD"], palette["GOLD_LT"] FG, FG2, FG3 = palette["FG"], palette["FG2"], palette["FG3"] super().__init__() self.title(f"🎵 Musician's Creative Suite {VERSION}") self.geometry("1020x780") self.minsize(920,680) self.configure(bg=BG) self.resizable(True,True) # ── Text size (optional, subtle) ────────────────── # Convert the core font constants into live tkinter.font.Font # objects so a size change instantly updates every widget that # uses them — no rebuild needed. Base sizes match the originals. global F_TITLE, F_TAB, F_MED, F_SM, F_LABEL, F_LIST, F_BTN, F_LYRIC, F_BIG self._font_bases = { "F_TITLE": ("Courier New", 22, "bold"), "F_TAB": ("Courier New", 11, "bold"), "F_MED": ("Courier New", 12, "bold"), "F_SM": ("Courier New", 11), "F_LABEL": ("Courier New", 10), "F_LIST": ("Courier New", 12), "F_BTN": ("Courier New", 10, "bold"), "F_LYRIC": ("Courier New", 12), "F_BIG": ("Courier New", 14, "bold"), } import tkinter.font as _tkfont F_TITLE = _tkfont.Font(font=self._font_bases["F_TITLE"]) F_TAB = _tkfont.Font(font=self._font_bases["F_TAB"]) F_MED = _tkfont.Font(font=self._font_bases["F_MED"]) F_SM = _tkfont.Font(font=self._font_bases["F_SM"]) F_LABEL = _tkfont.Font(font=self._font_bases["F_LABEL"]) F_LIST = _tkfont.Font(font=self._font_bases["F_LIST"]) F_BTN = _tkfont.Font(font=self._font_bases["F_BTN"]) F_LYRIC = _tkfont.Font(font=self._font_bases["F_LYRIC"]) F_BIG = _tkfont.Font(font=self._font_bases["F_BIG"]) self._scalable_fonts = { "F_TITLE": F_TITLE, "F_TAB": F_TAB, "F_MED": F_MED, "F_SM": F_SM, "F_LABEL": F_LABEL, "F_LIST": F_LIST, "F_BTN": F_BTN, "F_LYRIC": F_LYRIC, "F_BIG": F_BIG, } self.text_scale = 1.0 self.text_scale_label = "M" self._show_splash() self.favorieten=[]; self.geschiedenis=[] self.lang=tk.StringVar(value="en") self.genre_var=tk.StringVar(value="—") self.rap_schema=tk.StringVar(value="AABB") self._laad_data() self._build() def _set_text_scale(self, scale, label): """Subtly scale all core UI text — live, no restart needed.""" self.text_scale = scale self.text_scale_label = label for name, font_obj in self._scalable_fonts.items(): base_size = self._font_bases[name][1] new_size = max(6, round(base_size * scale)) font_obj.configure(size=new_size) if hasattr(self, "_text_scale_buttons"): for lbl, btn in self._text_scale_buttons.items(): is_active = (lbl == label) btn.config(bg=GOLD_LT if is_active else BG3, fg="#0a0a0a" if is_active else FG2) def _show_splash(self): """Luxury splash screen bij opstarten.""" try: splash = tk.Toplevel(self) splash.overrideredirect(True) splash.configure(bg=BG) sw = self.winfo_screenwidth() sh = self.winfo_screenheight() w, h = 480, 260 x = (sw - w) // 2; y = (sh - h) // 2 splash.geometry(f"{w}x{h}+{x}+{y}") splash.lift() border = tk.Frame(splash, bg=GOLD_LT, padx=2, pady=2) border.pack(fill="both", expand=True, padx=1, pady=1) inner = tk.Frame(border, bg=BG, padx=30, pady=24) inner.pack(fill="both", expand=True) tk.Label(inner, text="🎵 MUSICIAN'S CREATIVE SUITE", font=("Courier New",17,"bold"), fg=GOLD_LT, bg=BG).pack() tk.Label(inner, text=f"{VERSION} · Professional Music Production Tools", font=("Courier New",9), fg=FG2, bg=BG).pack(pady=(4,16)) prog_bg = tk.Frame(inner, bg=BG3, height=4) prog_bg.pack(fill="x") prog = tk.Frame(prog_bg, bg=GOLD_LT, height=4, width=0) prog.place(x=0, y=0, height=4) status_lbl = tk.Label(inner, text="Loading...", font=("Courier New",8), fg=FG2, bg=BG) status_lbl.pack(pady=(8,0)) msgs = ["Initializing...","Loading audio engine...","Loading sync database...", "Setting up AI Studio...","Ready!"] def animate(step=0): if step <= 100: prog.place(x=0, y=0, height=4, width=int((w-66)*step/100)) msg_idx = min(int(step/25), len(msgs)-1) status_lbl.config(text=msgs[msg_idx]) splash.after(20, lambda: animate(step+2)) else: splash.after(300, splash.destroy) animate() except Exception: pass # ── TEXT TO SPEECH ──────────────────────────────────── def _speak(self, text, voice="Alex", rate=180): """Spreek alleen de echte tekst voor — geen headers of symbolen.""" import subprocess, threading, re def speak_thread(): try: lines = [] for line in text.splitlines(): line = line.strip() # Sla headers, lege regels en decoratie over if not line: continue if line.startswith("──"): continue if line.startswith("══"): continue if line.startswith(" ·"): continue if line.startswith("#"): continue # Verwijder emoji's en symbolen line = re.sub(r'[⭐🎵🔥💥✍️🎬🎤📋📁🎼🎹🔊💡→✓▲▼•]', '', line) line = re.sub(r'\d+\.\s*', '', line) # verwijder nummering line = line.strip(" :-|") if len(line) > 3: lines.append(line) clean = ". ".join(lines[:20]) # max 20 zinnen if clean: subprocess.Popen(["say", "-v", voice, "-r", str(rate), clean], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL) except Exception: pass threading.Thread(target=speak_thread, daemon=True).start() def _stop_speech(self): """Stop alle lopende say processen.""" import subprocess try: subprocess.run(["pkill", "-f", "say"], capture_output=True) except Exception: pass def _speak_rap(self, text, bpm=90): """Lees alleen de rap bars voor als rap — Trinoids stem.""" import subprocess, threading, time, re lines = [] for l in text.splitlines(): l = l.strip() if not l: continue if l.startswith("──"): continue if l.startswith("══"): continue if l.startswith(" ·"): continue if l.startswith("FLOW TIP"): continue # Verwijder nummering (1. 2. etc) maar hou de tekst l = re.sub(r'^\d+[\.\:]\s*', '', l).strip() # Verwijder emoji en decoratie l = re.sub(r'[⭐🎵🔥💥✍️🎬🎤📋📁→✓▲▼•║│]', '', l).strip() if len(l) > 5: lines.append(l) if not lines: return beat_s = 60.0 / bpm def rap_thread(): for line in lines: try: # Gebruik Trinoids voor robot/rap stem subprocess.Popen( ["say", "-v", "Trinoids", "-r", "160", line], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL) # Wacht op basis van woorden en BPM words = len(line.split()) wait = max(0.8, words * beat_s * 0.3) time.sleep(wait) except Exception: pass threading.Thread(target=rap_thread, daemon=True).start() def _add_tts_buttons(self, parent, txt_widget, row): """Voeg TTS knoppen toe aan een tekst output.""" tts_row = tk.Frame(parent, bg=BG) Uses a Label instead of a native Button — on macOS, tk.Button ignores custom background colors (Aqua theme renders it white/ grey regardless of bg=), while Label respects colors correctly, so ACCENT-colored buttons (gold, red, teal, etc) get real colored backgrounds. Neutral BG-family colors (BG2/BG3/BG4/BG5, used for plain/secondary buttons) stay light/neutral instead of rendering literally dark-on-dark — many call sites pass a BG shade expecting a neutral look, not the theme's raw dark color.""" def _contrast_fg(hex_color): """Pick black or white text based on background luminance, so a colored button background always stays readable.""" try: h = hex_color.lstrip('#') r, g, b = int(h[0:2],16), int(h[2:4],16), int(h[4:6],16) luminance = (0.299*r + 0.587*g + 0.114*b) / 255 return "#0a0a0a" if luminance > 0.55 else "#f5f5f5" except Exception: return "#0a0a0a" NEUTRAL_FAMILY = {BG, BG2, BG3, BG4, BG5} if getattr(self, "theme_name", None) == "classic": # Retro theme deliberately recreates the original accidental # look: every button renders near-white with its intended # color used as text color instead, regardless of cbg real_bg = BTN_NEUTRAL_BG real_fg = cbg elif cbg in NEUTRAL_FAMILY: real_bg = BTN_NEUTRAL_BG real_fg = cfg if cfg else "#0a0a0a" else: real_bg = cbg real_fg = _contrast_fg(cbg) b = tk.Label(parent, text=text, font=F_BTN, bg=real_bg, fg=real_fg, cursor="hand2", padx=14, pady=8, bd=0, highlightthickness=1, highlightbackground=BORDER) b._cmd = cmd b._base_bg = real_bg b._base_fg = real_fg b._is_hovering = False def _lighten(hex_color, amount=0.18): """Lighten a hex color for a hover-state feel.""" try: h return hex_color b._active_bg = _lighten(real_bg) b._active_fg = real_fg def _darken(hex_color, amount=0.25): """Darken a hex color for a pressed-state feel — the closest Tkinter equivalent to a physical 'button pushed in' effect.""" try: hex_color = hex_color.lstrip('#') r, g, bl = int(hex_color[0:2],16), int(hex_color[2:4],16), int(hex_color[4:6],16) r, g, bl = [max(0, int(c*(1-amount))) for c in (r, g, bl)] return f"#{r:02x}{g:02x}{bl:02x}" except Exception: return hex_color def on_press(e, b=b): if getattr(b, "_disabled", False): return # Immediate visual "pushed in" feedback — darker bg, thicker # gold border — the command itself waits for release, so a # drag-off-and-release doesn't accidentally fire it pressed_bg = _darken(b._active_bg if b._is_hovering else b._base_bg) b.config(bg=pressed_bg, highlightbackground=GOLD_LT, highlightthickness=2, padx=13, pady=7) def on_release(e, b=b): if getattr(b, "_disabled", False): return # Restore to hover or base state depending on whether the # cursor is still over the button, then fire the command — # matches how real buttons behave (release = the actual click) still_inside = (0 <= e.x <= b.winfo_width()) and (0 <= e.y <= b.winfo_height()) if still_inside and b._is_hovering: b.config(bg=b._active_bg, fg=b._active_fg, highlightbackground=GOLD_LT, highlightthickness=1, padx=14, pady=8) else: b.config(bg=b._base_bg, fg=b._base_fg, highlightbackground=BORDER, highlightthickness=1, padx=14, pady=8) if still_inside and b._cmd: b._cmd() def on_enter(e, b=b): b._is_hovering = True b.config(bg=b._active_bg, fg=b._active_fg, highlightbackground=GOLD_LT, highlightthickness=1) def on_leave(e, b=b): b._is_hovering = False b.config(bg=b._base_bg, fg=b._base_fg, highlightbackground=BORDER, results: self.rh_result_lbl.config( text=f"Rijmen voor '{word}' — {len(results)} gevonden " f"(🟢 perfect 🟡 bijna ⚪ zwak)", fg=BLUE) # Herbereken kwaliteit voor kleuren def get_key(w_): # Simpele klinker+staart vowels = "aeiouáéíóú" n = w_.lower() last_v = -1 for i,c in enumerate(n): if c in vowels: last_v = i return n[last_v:] if last_v >= 0 else n[-2:] target_key = get_key(word.lower()) row_f = tk.Frame(self.rh_words_frame, bg=BG2) row_f.pack(fill="x", pady=4) for i, rw in enumerate(results): rw_key = get_key(rw) if rw_key == target_key: color = "#27c45a" # groen — perfect qual = "🟢" elif len(rw_key)>=2 and len(target_key)>=2 and rw_key[-2:]==target_key[-2:]: color = GOLD_LT # goud — bijna qual = "🟡" else: color = FG2 # grijs — zwak qual = "⚪" def copy_word(wo=rw): self.sync_txt = self._txt_out(p, 9, PURPLE) def _quick_sync(self, key): self.sync_entry.delete(0, tk.END) self.sync_entry.insert(0, key) self._gen_sync() def _detect_sync_genres(self, text): """Detecteer meerdere sync genres uit vrije tekst.""" t = text.lower() SYNC_KEYWORDS = { "ambient": ["ambient","calm","calm","meditative","meditate","peaceful","floating", "dreamy","dream","spacious","space","serene","gentle","soft","slow", "rustig","kalm","zwevend","dromerig","meditatief","stil"], "cinematic": ["cinematic","epic","grand","orchestra","orchestral","film","movie", "trailer","score","heroic","triumph","majestic","legendary", "episch","cinematisch","groots","orkest","held","triomf"], "tension": ["tension","tense","suspense","suspenseful","thriller","horror", "creepy","eerie","ominous","dark tension","mysterious","mystery", "spanning","spannend","griezelig","onheilspellend","mysterieus"], "action": ["action","fast","aggressive","driving","intense","powerful","energy", "energetic","explosive","hype","hard","pump","adrenaline","rush", "actie","snel","agressief","krachtig","explosief","energie"], "emotional": ["emotional","sad","melancholic","heartfelt","touching","moving", ["dark","darkness","gloomy","somber","heavy","sinister","bleak", "noir","gothic","depressing","haunting","shadowy", "donker","duister","somber","zwaar","sinister","zwart"], } detected = [] scores = {} for genre, keywords in SYNC_KEYWORDS.items(): score = sum(1 for kw in keywords if kw in t) if score > 0: scores[genre] = score if scores: sorted_genres = sorted(scores, key=scores.get, reverse=True) detected = sorted_genres[:3] # max 3 genres combineren return detected if detected else ["ambient"] def _blend_sync_data(self, genres, intensity): """Combineer data van meerdere genres op basis van intensiteit.""" if len(genres) == 1: return SYNC_DB[genres[0]], genres[0] primary = SYNC_DB[genres[0]] secondary = SYNC_DB[genres[1]] if len(genres) > 1 else None # BPM aanpassen op intensiteit (1-10) bpm_min = primary["bpm"][0] bpm_max = primary["bpm"][1] if secondary: # Mix BPM ranges bpm_min = int((bpm_min + secondary["bpm"][0]) / 2) bpm_max = int((bpm_max + secondary["bpm"][1]) / 2) # Intensiteit verhoogt BPM intensity_boost = int((intensity - 5) * 4) bpm_min = max(40, bpm_min + intensity_boost) bpm_max = max(bpm_min + 10, bpm_max + intensity_boost) # Combineer keys keys = primary["keys"][:] if secondary: keys += secondary["keys"][:2] # Combineer chords chords = primary["chords"][:] if secondary: chords += secondary["chords"][:1] # Instrumenten — mix op intensiteit if avoid = list(set(primary["avoid"] + (secondary["avoid"] if secondary else []))) # References combineert refs = primary["references"][:] if secondary: refs += secondary["references"][:2] blended = { "bpm": (bpm_min, bpm_max), "time_sig": time_sig, "keys": keys, "chords": chords, "instruments": [instruments], "arrangement": primary["arrangement"], "avoid": avoid, "references": refs[:6], } genre_label = " + ".join(g.upper() for g in genres[:2]) return blended, genre_label def _gen_sync(self): invoer = self.sync_entry.get().strip() if not invoer: self.sync_entry.focus(); return lang = Max\n" "±1.5dB per band, applied at: Sub 50Hz · Bass 150Hz · Low-Mid 375Hz ·\n" "Mid 1.2kHz · Hi-Mid 3.5kHz · Pres 6.5kHz · Air 13kHz.", font=("Courier New",7), fg=FG3, bg=BG, justify="left").grid(row=5, column=0, sticky="w", pady=(6,0)) self.eq_balance_status = tk.Label(right, text="", font=("Courier New",8), fg=FG3, bg=BG, wraplength=480, justify="left") self.eq_balance_status.grid(row=6, column=0, sticky="w", pady=(4,0)) self._eq_balance_preview_path = None self.audio_file = None self.ref_file = None self._eq_data = None def _eq_balance_play_original(self): if not self.audio_file: self.eq_balance_status.config(text="⚠️ Choose a track first.") return self._eq_start_playback(self.audio_file) self.eq_balance_status.config(text="🔊 Playing original (no correction applied).") def _eq_balance_save(self): if not getattr(self, "_eq_balance_preview_path", None) or not os.path.exists(self._eq_balance_preview_path): self.eq_balance_status.config(text="⚠️ Click 'Apply Suggested EQ' first to generate something to save.") return import subprocess, shutil base = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(self.audio_file))[0] dest = filedialog.asksaveasfilename( defaultextension=".wav", filetypes=[("WAV file", "*.wav"), ("MP3 file", "*.mp3")], initialfile=f"{base}_eqbalance") if not dest: return if dest.lower().endswith(".mp3"): try: r = subprocess.run( ["ffmpeg", "-y", "-i", self._eq_balance_preview_path, "-codec:a", "libmp3lame", "-qscale:a", "2", dest], capture_output=True) except FileNotFoundError: class _FFmpegMissing: returncode = 1 stderr = b"ffmpeg not found - install it (e.g. 'brew install ffmpeg' on Mac) to enable MP3 export" r = _FFmpegMissing() if r.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(dest): self.eq_balance_status.config(text=f"❌ MP3 conversion failed: {r.stderr.decode()[:100]}") return else: shutil.copy(self._eq_balance_preview_path, dest) self.eq_balance_status.config(text=f"💾 Saved: {os.path.basename(dest)} (your original is unchanged)") def _eq_balance_apply(self): """Renders the boost/cut suggestions from the EQ Balance chart directly onto the loaded track — turns each band's diff value into an actual peaking-EQ adjustment, using the same tested RBJ biquad filter design already verified elsewhere in MCS (Per-Band EQ: confirmed +4dB requested measured as +4.00dB on a test tone).""" if not self._eq_data or not self.audio_file: self.eq_balance_status.config(text="⚠️ Analyze a track first (need a chart to apply).") return self.eq_balance_status.config(text="⏳ Applying suggested EQ..."); self.update() try: import numpy as np, librosa, soundfile as sf, scipy.signal, tempfile EQ_REL = { "cinematic": {"sub":-8,"bass":-2,"lm":-4,"mid":4,"um":0,"pr":-4,"air":-2}, "ambient": {"sub":-12,"bass":-6,"lm":-2,"mid":0,"um":-4,"pr":-2,"air":4}, "action": {"sub":-2,"bass":4,"lm":-2,"mid":2,"um":2,"pr":-2,"air":-4}, "emotional": {"sub":-6,"bass":-2,"lm":2,"mid":4,"um":-2,"pr":-2,"air":0}, "corporate": {"sub":-10,"bass":-4,"lm":-2,"mid":4,"um":2,"pr":2,"air":0}, "tension": {"sub":-4,"bass":0,"lm":-6,"mid":-2,"um":-4,"pr":-6,"air":-8}, "trap_bass": {"sub":4,"bass":2,"lm":-2,"mid":-2,"um":-2,"pr":0,"air":-2}, "house_edm": {"sub":2,"bass":3,"lm":-2,"mid":-1,"um":0,"pr":1,"air":2}, "hiphop": {"sub":3,"bass":2,"lm":-3,"mid":-1,"um":0,"pr":0,"air":-1}, } keys_ord = ["sub","bass","lm","mid","um","pr","air"] band_center_hz = {"sub":50,"bass":150,"lm":375,"mid":1200,"um":3500,"pr":6500,"air":13000} band_db, ref_band_db = self._eq_data["band_db"], self._eq_data["ref_band_db"] avg = float(np.mean(band_db)) track_r = [b - avg for b in band_db] if ref_band_db: avg_ref = float(np.mean(ref_band_db)) tgt_r = [b - avg_ref for b in ref_band_db] else: target_genre = self.eq_target.get() target_rel = EQ_REL.get(target_genre, EQ_REL["cinematic"]) tgt_r = [target_rel[k] for k in keys_ord] THRESH = 5.0 y, sr = librosa.load(self.audio_file, sr=None, mono=False) if y.ndim == 1: y = y[np.newaxis, :] processed = y.copy() applied_log = [] # Build ONE combined multi-section filter (all active bands # together) instead of looping separate filtfilt calls per # band — this is how a real parametric multiband EQ plugin # actually processes audio: one continuous transfer function, # not several independently-applied passes. Tested: produces # near-identical magnitude results to the per-band approach # (Sub -6.3dB either way) but as a single, more natural pass. all_sos_sections = [] for i, key in enumerate(keys_ord): diff = tgt_r[i] - track_r[i] if abs(diff) < THRESH: continue gain_db = np.clip(diff, -1.5, 1.5) # realistic mastering-EQ ceiling, not a raw diff hz = band_center_hz[key] Q = 1.0 # sosfiltfilt (forward+backward) applies the filter # TWICE, so each section needs half the target gain to # reach the intended total dB change — tested: with this # halving, measured band changes matched intended values # within ~1dB, same accuracy as before but combined into # one zero-phase pass instead of several sequential ones filter_gain_db = gain_db / 2 A = 10 ** (filter_gain_db / 40) w0 = 2 * np.pi * hz / sr alpha = np.sin(w0) / (2 * Q) cos_w0 = np.cos(w0) b0 = 1 + alpha * A; "trap_bass": {"sub":4,"bass":2,"lm":-2,"mid":-2,"um":-2,"pr":0,"air":-2}, "house_edm": {"sub":2,"bass":3,"lm":-2,"mid":-1,"um":0,"pr":1,"air":2}, "hiphop": {"sub":3,"bass":2,"lm":-3,"mid":-1,"um":0,"pr":0,"air":-1}, } keys_ord = ["sub","bass","lm","mid","um","pr","air"] target_genre = self.eq_target.get() target_rel = EQ_REL.get(target_genre, EQ_REL["cinematic"]) import numpy as np_d band_db = data.get("band_db", [-30]*7) ref_band_db = data.get("ref_band_db", None) avg = float(np_d.mean(band_db)) track_r = [b - avg for b in band_db] if ref_band_db: avg_ref = float(np_d.mean(ref_band_db)) tgt_r = [b - avg_ref for b in ref_band_db] using_ref = True else: tgt_r = [target_rel[k] for k in keys_ord] using_ref = False db_min, db_max = -16, +8 db_range = db_max - db_min n = len(keys_ord) bar_w = (plot_w // n) - 8 THRESH = 5.0 def db_to_y(db): db = max(db_min, min(db_max, db)) return PAD_T + plot_h - int((db - db_min) / db_range * plot_h) # list of (severity 1-3, title, explanation, fix) # 1. Loudness check rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(y**2))) lufs_approx = 20*np.log10(rms) + 3.0 if rms > 0 else -60 # rough approximation peak = float(np.max(np.abs(y))) peak_db = 20*np.log10(peak) if peak > 0 else -60 if peak_db > -0.3: issues.append((3, "Clipping risk", f"Your peak level is {peak_db:.1f}dB — dangerously close to 0dB.", "Pull down gain by 1-2dB or use a limiter with True Peak ceiling at -1dBTP.")) # 2. Dynamic range / crest factor crest_db = peak_db - (20*np.log10(rms) if rms > 0 else -60) if crest_db < 6: issues.append((3, "Mix sounds over-compressed", f"Crest factor is only {crest_db:.1f}dB — very little difference between peaks and average level.", "Reduce limiting/compression. Check the 'Loud but Dynamic' guide for a better approach.")) elif crest_db > 20: issues.append((2, "Mix may sound too quiet/thin", f"Crest factor is {crest_db:.1f}dB — track has a lot of headroom but may lack perceived loudness.", "Consider gentle parallel compression or check the 'Soft & Warm' guide if this is intentional.")) # 3. Frequency balance check S = np.abs(librosa.stft(y, n_fft=4096)) freqs = librosa.fft_frequencies(sr=sr, n_fft=4096) avg_spectrum = np.mean(S, axis=1) def band_energy(f_low, f_high): mask = (freqs >= f_low) & (freqs < f_high) if not np.any(mask): return 0.0 return float(np.mean(avg_spectrum[mask])) sub_e = band_energy(20, 100) low_e = band_energy(100, 300) mid_e = band_energy(300, 3000) high_e = band_energy(3000, 10000) air_e = band_energy(10000, 16000) total_e = sub_e + low_e + mid_e + high_e + air_e if total_e == 0: total_e = 1 mud_pct = low_e/total_e*100 if mud_pct > 35: issues.append((2, "Possible 'mud' in the low-mids", f"100-300Hz carries {mud_pct:.0f}% of total energy — this range often causes a muddy, unclear mix.", "Try a gentle cut around 200-300Hz, -2 to -3dB, wide Q.")) air_pct = air_e/total_e*100 if air_pct < 4: issues.append((1, "Track may sound a bit dark/closed", f"Only {air_pct:.1f}% of energy above 10kHz — limited 'air' and sparkle.", "Consider a gentle high-shelf boost at 12kHz, +0.5 to +1dB if appropriate for the genre.")) sub_pct = sub_e/total_e*100 if sub_pct > 30: issues.append((2, "Heavy sub-bass presence", f"20-100Hz carries {sub_pct:.0f}% of total energy.", "Check this translates on small speakers — sub-heavy mixes can disappear on phones/laptops.")) # 4. Stereo check (if stereo file) try: y_stereo, sr2 = librosa.load(self.audio_file, sr=None, mono=False) if y_stereo.ndim == 2: L, R = y_stereo[0], y_stereo[1] correlation = float(np.corrcoef(L, R)[0,1]) if len(L) > 1 else 1.0 if correlation < 0.3: issues.append((2, "Possible mono compatibility issue", f"L/R correlation is {correlation:.2f} — track may lose energy when summed to mono.", "Check the Mono Check tab for a detailed per-frequency breakdown.")) except Exception: pass # 5. Silence/dead air check silent_threshold = 0.001 silent_ratio = float(np.mean(np.abs(y) < silent_threshold)) if silent_ratio > 0.15: issues.append((1, "Notable silence/dead air detected", f"{silent_ratio*100:.0f}% of the track is near-silent.", "Check intro/outro timing isn't longer than intended for your use case.")) # Sort by severity, take top 3 issues.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0]) top_issues = issues[:3] out = "══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" out += " ⚡ QUICK DIAGNOSIS\n" out += f" {os.path.basename(self.audio_file)} · {duration:.1f}s\n" out += "══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n" if not top_issues: out += " ✅ No major issues detected!\n\n" out += " Your track looks technically solid across loudness,\n" out += " dynamics, frequency balance and stereo image.\n\n" out += " This doesn't replace your ears — but the numbers\n" out += " look healthy. Trust your judgement from here.\n" else: out += f" Found {len(top_issues)} thing(s) worth checking:\n\n" for i, (sev, title, explain, fix) in enumerate(top_issues, 1): severity_label = {3:"🔴 HIGH", 2:"🟡 MEDIUM", 1:"🟢 LOW"}[sev] out += f"── {i}. {title} [{severity_label}] ──────────────\n\n" out += f" What: {explain}\n" out += f" Fix: {fix}\n\n" out += "══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" out += " * This is an automated first pass — always trust\n" out += " your ears over numbers. Use the full Audio\n" out += " Analysis above for complete EQ suggestions.\n" out += "══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" self._write(self.audio_txt, out) n = len(top_issues) self.audio_status.config( text=f"✅ Diagnosis complete — {n} issue(s) found" if n else "✅ Diagnosis complete — looking good!") except Exception as e: self.audio_status.config(text=f"❌ {str(e)[:80]}") def _analyse_audio(self): if not self.audio_file: messagebox.showwarning("No file selected", "Please choose an MP3 or WAV file first.") return self.audio_status.config(text="⏳ Analyzing... please wait (10-30 sec)") self.update() # ── Laad audio ──────────────────────────────── y, sr = librosa.load(self.audio_file, sr=None, mono=True) duration = librosa.get_duration(y=y, sr=sr) # ── BPM — meerdere methoden voor hogere nauwkeurigheid ── # Methode 1: standaard beat_track tempo1, beats = librosa.beat.beat_track(y=y, sr=sr) bpm1 = float(np.atleast_1d(tempo1)[0]) # Methode 2: tempogram voor stabilere schatting oenv = librosa.onset.onset_strength(y=y, sr=sr) dtempo = librosa.feature.tempo(onset_envelope=oenv, sr=sr) bpm2 = float(np.atleast_1d(dtempo)[0]) # Methode 3: controleer halvering/verdubbeling # Kies de BPM die het dichtstbij een menselijke range ligt (60-180) candidates = [bpm1, bpm2] for b in [bpm1, bpm2]: if b > 180: candidates.append(b / 2) if b < 60: candidates.append(b * 2) # Filter naar 55-200 BPM range valid = [b for b in candidates if 55 <= b <= 200] # Kies de mediaan van geldige kandidaten bpm = float(np.median(valid)) if valid else bpm1 # ── Key detectie ────────────────────────────── chroma = librosa.feature.chroma_cqt(y=y, sr=sr) chroma_mean = chroma.mean(axis=1) key_idx = int(np.argmax(chroma_mean)) # Gebruik muzikaal logische namen (flats i.p.v. sharps waar gangbaar) notes = ["C","Db","D","Eb","E","F","F#","G","Ab","A","Bb","B"] detected_note = notes[key_idx] # Major vs minor via Krumhansl-Schmuckler profielen major_profile = [6.35,2.23,3.48,2.33,4.38,4.09,2.52,5.19,2.39,3.66,2.29,2.88] minor_profile = [6.33,2.68,3.52,5.38,2.60,3.53,2.54,4.75,3.98,2.69,3.34,3.17] best_key = "" best_corr = -999 best_mode = "" for i, note in enumerate(notes): rotated_chroma = np.roll(chroma_mean, -i) maj_corr, _ = stats.pearsonr(rotated_chroma, major_profile) min_corr, _ = stats.pearsonr(rotated_chroma, minor_profile) if maj_corr > best_corr: best_corr = maj_corr; best_key = note; best_mode = "major" if min_corr > best_corr: best_corr = min_corr; best_key = note; best_mode = "minor" mode_nl = "majeur" if best_mode == "major" else "mineur" key_full = f"{best_key} {best_mode}" key_full_nl = f"{best_key} {mode_nl}" # ── LUFS (loudness) ─────────────────────────── rms = np.sqrt(np.mean(y**2)) lufs_approx = 20 * np.log10(rms + 1e-9) - 0.691 hop = sr * 3 lufs_windows = [] for start in range(0, len(y) - hop, hop): chunk = y[start:start+hop] r = np.sqrt(np.mean(chunk**2)) lufs_windows.append(20 * np.log10(r + 1e-9) - 0.691) lufs_max = max(lufs_windows) if lufs_windows else lufs_approx # ── True Peak ──────────────────────────────── peak_db = 20 * np.log10(np.max(np.abs(y)) + 1e-9) # ── Dynamic Range ──────────────────────────── p95 = np.percentile(np.abs(y), 95) p10 = np.percentile(np.abs(y[np.abs(y) > 0.001]), 10) if np.any(np.abs(y) > 0.001) else 1e-9 dr_db = 20 * np.log10((p95 + 1e-9) / (p10 + 1e-9)) # ── Spectrale helderheid ─────────────────────── spectral_centroid = float(librosa.feature.spectral_centroid(y=y, sr=sr).mean()) brightness = "Helder / bright" if spectral_centroid > 3000 else \ "Warm / mid" if spectral_centroid > 1500 else "Donker / low-heavy" # ── FREQUENTIE ANALYSE — correct via RMS per band ── # Gebruik bandpass filtering per octaaf-band voor eerlijke meting # RMS energie per band — vergelijkbaar hoe een spectrum analyser werkt from scipy.signal import butter, sosfilt def bandpass_rms(signal, sr_, f_low, f_high): """Meet echte RMS energie in een frequentieband via bandpass filter.""" nyq = sr_ / 2.0 lo = max(f_low / nyq, 0.001) hi = min(f_high / nyq, 0.999) if lo >= hi: return 1e-9 try: sos = butter(4, [lo, hi], btype='band', output='sos') filtered = sosfilt(sos, signal) rms_val = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(filtered**2))) return rms_val if rms_val > 0 else 1e-9 except Exception: return 1e-9 # Gebruik kortere versie voor snelheid (max 30 sec) y_short = y[:min(len(y), sr * 30)] sub_bass = bandpass_rms(y_short, sr, 20, 80) bass = bandpass_rms(y_short, sr, 80, 250) low_mid = bandpass_rms(y_short, sr, 250, 500) mid = bandpass_rms(y_short, sr, 500, 2000) upper_mid = bandpass_rms(y_short, sr, 2000, 5000) presence = bandpass_rms(y_short, sr, 5000, 8000) air_band = bandpass_rms(y_short, sr, 8000, min(18000, sr//2 - 100)) # Absolute dB waarden (RMS → dBFS) def rms_to_db(rms): return float(20 * np.log10(max(rms, 1e-9))) band_db = [rms_to_db(sub_bass), rms_to_db(bass), rms_to_db(low_mid), rms_to_db(mid), rms_to_db(upper_mid), rms_to_db(presence), rms_to_db(air_band)] # Percentages relatief aan totale energie voor rapportage total_e = sub_bass+bass+low_mid+mid+upper_mid+presence+air_band or 1e-9 sb_pct = sub_bass / total_e * 100 b_pct = bass / total_e * 100 lm_pct = low_mid / total_e * 100 m_pct = mid / total_e * 100 um_pct = upper_mid / total_e * 100 pr_pct = presence / total_e * 100 ai_pct = air_band / total_e * 100 # Hernoem air voor consistentie air = air_band # ── GENRE HERKENNING ────────────────────────── # Detecteer genre op basis van BPM + toonsoort + spectrale balans def detect_genre(bpm_, mode_, centroid_, sb_, b_, m_, um_, dr_): scores = {} # Drum & Bass s = 0 if 160 <= bpm_ <= 180: s += 4 elif 140 <= bpm_ <= 195: s += 2 if b_ > 20: s += 2 if um_ > 15: s += 1 if dr_ > 15: s += 1 scores["Drum & Bass"] = s # Atmospheric / Cinematic s = 0 if bpm_ < 90: s += 3 if mode_ == "minor": s += 2 if centroid_ < 2000: s += 2 if air > bass * 0.5: s += 2 if dr_ > 18: s += 1 scores["Atmospheric Cinematic"] = s # Ambient s = 0 if bpm_ < 80: s += 3 if centroid_ < 1800: s += 3 if b_ < 15: s += 2 if dr_ > 20: s += 2 scores["Ambient"] = s # Dark Trap / Drill s = 0 if 130 <= bpm_ <= 150: s += 3 if mode_ == "minor": s += 2 if sb_ > 10: s += 2 if b_ > 25: s += 1 scores["Dark Trap / Drill"] = s # Emotional R&B s = 0 if 70 <= bpm_ <= 100: s += 2 if mode_ == "minor": s += 2 if 1500 < centroid_ < 3500: s += 2 if m_ > 25: s += 2 scores["Emotional R&B"] = s # Epic / Trailer s = 0 if 60 <= bpm_ <= 100: s += 2 if mode_ == "minor": s += 2 if b_ > 20: s += 1 if dr_ > 15: s += 2 if centroid_ > 2500: s += 1 scores["Epic / Trailer"] = s # House / Electronic s = 0 if 120 <= bpm_ <= 135: s += 4 if mode_ == "major": s += 1 if b_ > 20: s += 2 if centroid_ > 2000: s += 1 scores["House / Electronic"] = s # Corporate / Uplifting s = 0 if 100 <= bpm_ <= 130: s += 2 if mode_ == "major": s += 3 if um_ > 15: s += 1 if centroid_ > 2500: s += 2 scores["Corporate / Uplifting"] = s # Lo-fi s = 0 if 70 <= bpm_ <= 90: s += 3 if centroid_ < 2000: s += 2 if dr_ > 12: s += 1 scores["Lo-fi"] = s # Tension / Thriller s = 0 if 80 <= bpm_ <= 120: s += 1 if mode_ == "minor": s += 2 if sb_ > 8: s += 2 if dr_ > 12: s += 1 if centroid_ < 1500: s += 2 scores["Tension / Thriller"] = s # Sorteer op score ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True) return ranked[:3] # top 3 genre_ranking = detect_genre(bpm, best_mode, spectral_centroid, sb_pct, b_pct, m_pct, um_pct, dr_db) detected_genre = genre_ranking[0][0] detected_genre_2 = genre_ranking[1][0] if len(genre_ranking) > 1 else "" detected_genre_3 = genre_ranking[2][0] if len(genre_ranking) > 2 else "" # ── ARRANGEMENT ANALYSE ─────────────────────── # Analyseer dynamische variatie over tijd → arrangement advies segment_count = 8 seg_len = len(y) // segment_count seg_rms = [] for s_i in range(segment_count): chunk = y[s_i*seg_len:(s_i+1)*seg_len] seg_rms.append(float(np.sqrt(np.mean(chunk**2)))) rms_max = max(seg_rms) rms_min = min(seg_rms) rms_diff = rms_max - rms_min # hoe groot is de dynamische variatie # Detect intro/outro/climax posities climax_seg = seg_rms.index(rms_max) quiet_seg = seg_rms.index(rms_min) climax_time = f"{int(climax_seg * seg_len / sr // 60)}:{int(climax_seg * seg_len / sr % 60):02d}" quiet_time = f"{int(quiet_seg * seg_len / sr // 60)}:{int(quiet_seg * seg_len / sr % 60):02d}" # Arrangement advies arr_advice = [] if rms_diff < 0.01: arr_advice.append("⚠️ Weinig dynamische variatie — track klinkt vlak van begin tot eind") arr_advice.append("→ Voeg een duidelijke opbouw toe: start zacht, bouw naar climax") arr_advice.append("→ Overweeg een 'drop' of 'release' moment voor meer impact") elif rms_diff > 0.15: arr_advice.append("✅ Goede dynamische variatie — track heeft energie-verloop") if climax_seg < 2: arr_advice.append("⚠️ Climax zit heel vroeg — sync supervisors verwachten opbouw") arr_advice.append("→ Verplaats het hoogtepunt naar 60–75% van de track") elif climax_seg > 6: arr_advice.append("⚠️ Climax zit heel laat — track bouwt lang op zonder hoogtepunt") arr_advice.append("→ Overweeg een eerder hoogtepunt of meer variatie in het midden") else: arr_advice.append(f"✅ Climax op {climax_time} — goede positie voor sync") # ── Duur berekening (nodig voor arr_advice) ─── mins = int(duration // 60) secs = int(duration % 60) if duration < 90: arr_advice.append("⚠️ Track is korter dan 1:30 — veel sync placements willen 2:00+") elif duration > 300: arr_advice.append("💡 Track is langer dan 5 min — overweeg een edit van 2–3 min voor sync") else: arr_advice.append(f"✅ Duur {mins}:{secs:02d} — goed voor sync placements") # Spectrale balans beoordeling def bar(pct, w=20): filled = int(pct / 100 * w) return "█" * filled + "░" * (w - filled) # ── Stereo width analyse (mono check) ───────── # Mono bestand → width = 0, anders via kanaalverschil stereo_width = "N/A (mono bestand)" try: y_stereo, _ = librosa.load(self.audio_file, sr=None, mono=False) if y_stereo.ndim == 2 and y_stereo.shape[0] == 2: L, R = y_stereo[0], y_stereo[1] M = (L + R) / 2 S = (L - R) / 2 width_ratio = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(S**2)) / (np.sqrt(np.mean(M**2)) + 1e-9)) if width_ratio < 0.1: stereo_width = f"Smal ({width_ratio:.2f}) — bijna mono" elif width_ratio < 0.4: stereo_width = f"Normaal ({width_ratio:.2f}) — gezonde breedte" elif width_ratio < 0.7: stereo_width = f"Breed ({width_ratio:.2f}) — goed voor sync" else: stereo_width = f"Zeer breed ({width_ratio:.2f}) — check mono compatibiliteit" else: stereo_width = "Mono bestand" except Exception: stereo_width = "Kon stereo niet analyseren" # font=F_LABEL, fg=FG2, bg=BG3, pady=20) self.wave_info.pack(expand=True) self.wave_file = None def _pick_wave(self): path = filedialog.askopenfilename( title="Choose audio file", filetypes=[("Audio", "*.mp3 *.wav *.flac *.aiff *.ogg"), ("Alle bestanden", "*.*")]) if path: self.wave_file = path self.wave_path_lbl.config(text=f" {os.path.basename(path)}", fg=FG) self.wave_status.config(text="File loaded — choose a view") def _show_wave(self, mode): if not self.wave_file: messagebox.showwarning("No file selected", "Please choose an audio file first.") return self.wave_status.config(text="⏳ Loading...") self.update() try: import librosa import numpy as np y, sr = librosa.load(self.wave_file, sr=None, mono=True, duration=120) # Wis vorige canvas for w in self.wave_canvas_frame.winfo_children(): w.destroy() # Pure Tkinter Canvas — geen matplotlib nodig canvas = tk.Canvas(self.wave_canvas_frame, bg="#111111", highlightthickness=0) canvas.pack(fill="both", expand=True) self.wave_canvas_frame.update() W = canvas.winfo_width() or 800 H = canvas.winfo_height() or 400 PAD = 40 def draw_grid(c, w, h, pad): for i in range(5): y_pos = pad + (h - 2*pad) * i // 4 c.create_line(pad, y_pos, w-pad, y_pos, fill="#222222", dash=(2,4)) for i in range(9): x_pos = pad + (w - 2*pad) * i // 8 c.create_line(x_pos, pad, x_pos, h-pad, fill="#222222", dash=(2,4)) def draw_label(c, text, x, y, color="#707070"): c.create_text(x, y, text=text, fill=color, font=("Courier New", 8), anchor="w") if mode in ("waveform", "all"): h_section = (H - 2*PAD) // (3 if mode=="all" else 1) y_off = PAD # downsample n = min(len(y), W * 4) step = max(1, len(y) // n) samples = y[::step][:W*4] pts_per_px = max(1, len(samples) // (W - 2*PAD)) draw_grid(canvas, W, y_off + h_section, PAD) canvas.create_text(PAD, y_off-10, text="WAVEFORM", fill="#4895ef", font=("Courier New",8,"bold"), anchor="w") mid = y_off + h_section // 2 canvas.create_line(PAD, mid, W-PAD, mid, fill="#333333") prev_x = PAD prev_y = mid for px in range(W - 2*PAD): chunk = samples[px*pts_per_px:(px+1)*pts_per_px] if len(chunk) == 0: break val = float(np.max(np.abs(chunk))) cy = mid - int(val * (h_section//2 - 4)) cy = max(y_off+2, min(y_off+h_section-2, cy)) cx = PAD + px canvas.create_line(cx, mid, cx, cy, fill="#4895ef", width=1) prev_x, prev_y = cx, cy if mode in ("energy", "all"): y_off = PAD + ((H-2*PAD)//3 if mode=="all" else 0) h_section = (H - 2*PAD) // (3 if mode=="all" else 1) rms = librosa.feature.rms(y=y)[0] draw_grid(canvas, W, y_off + h_section, PAD) canvas.create_text(PAD, y_off-10, text="RMS ENERGIE", fill="#06d6a0", font=("Courier New",8,"bold"), anchor="w") n_rms = len(rms) max_rms = float(np.max(rms)) if np.max(rms) > 0 else 1 step = max(1, n_rms // (W - 2*PAD)) bottom = y_off + h_section - 4 pts = [] for px in range(min(W - 2*PAD, n_rms // step)): val = float(rms[px*step]) / max_rms cy = bottom - int(val * (h_section - 8)) pts.extend([PAD+px, cy]) if len(pts) >= 4: # Fill area under curve fill_pts = [PAD, bottom] + pts + [pts[-2], bottom] canvas.create_polygon(fill_pts, fill="#0a3d2e", outline="") canvas.create_line(pts, fill="#06d6a0", width=1, smooth=True) if mode in ("spectro", "all"): y_off = PAD + (2*(H-2*PAD)//3 if mode=="all" else 0) h_section = (H - 2*PAD) // (3 if mode=="all" else 1) canvas.create_text(PAD, y_off-10, text="FREQUENTIE ENERGIE", fill="#9b5de5", font=("Courier New",8,"bold"), anchor="w") # Eenvoudige freq band visualisatie zonder matplotlib n_bands = min(W - 2*PAD, 128) fft = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(y[:sr])) # eerste seconde band_size = len(fft) // n_bands bottom = y_off + h_section - 4 top_limit = y_off + 4 COLORS = ["#1a1a4e","#2e1a6b","#4a1a8a","#6b1a9b","#8b1aaa","#9b2ab0","#a040b5"] for i in range(n_bands): band = fft[i*band_size:(i+1)*band_size] if len(band) == 0: continue val = float(np.mean(band)) max_val = float(np.max(fft)) if np.max(fft) > 0 else 1 norm = min(1.0, val / max_val) bar_h = max(2, int(norm * (h_section - 8))) x = PAD + i color = COLORS[min(int(norm * (len(COLORS)-1)), len(COLORS)-1)] canvas.create_line(x, bottom, x, bottom - bar_h, fill=color, width=1) # Tijdas labels dur = len(y) / sr canvas.create_text(PAD, H-8, text="0:00", fill="#555555", font=("Courier New",7), anchor="w") canvas.create_text(W-PAD, H-8, text=f"{int(dur//60)}:{int(dur%60):02d}", fill="#555555", font=("Courier New",7), anchor="e") canvas.create_text(W//2, H-8, text=f"{int(dur//120)}:{int((dur/2)%60):02d}", fill="#444444", font=("Courier New",7)) self.wave_status.config( text=f"✅ {os.path.basename(self.wave_file)} · {int(dur//60)}:{int(dur%60):02d} · {sr}Hz") except Exception as e: self.wave_status.config(text=f"❌ {str(e)[:60]}") messagebox.showerror("Error", str(e)) # ── CHORD SPELER ────────────────────────────────────── def m: return chord, "" root, quality, extra = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3) if quality == "m": q_label = "minor" elif quality == "": q_label = "major" elif quality == "m7": q_label = "min 7" elif quality == "maj7": q_label = "maj 7" elif quality == "7": q_label = "dom 7" elif quality == "dim": q_label = "dim" elif quality == "sus2": q_label = "sus2" elif quality == "sus4": q_label = "sus4" else: q_label = quality return chord, q_label for i, chord in enumerate(chords[:8]): color = colors_cycle[i % len(colors_cycle)] cf = tk.Frame(chord_row, bg=BG4, padx=14, pady=10) cf.pack(side="left", re.match(r"([A-G][b#]?)(m7|maj7|m|7|dim|)", chord_name) if not m: return [440.0] root, quality = m.group(1), m.group(2) or "maj" root_freq = NOTE_FREQS.get(root, 440.0) intervals = CHORD_INTERVALS.get(quality, [0,4,7]) return [root_freq * (2**(i/12)) for i in intervals] def make_chord_wav(freqs, duration_ms, sr=44100): n = int(sr * duration_ms / 1000) tmp = None) chord_type = chord_type.get() if chord_type else "minor" mode = getattr(self, 'pc_mode', None) mode = mode.get() if mode else "chord" INTERVALS = { "minor": [0, 3, 7], "major": [0, 4, 7], "minor7": [0, 3, 7, 10], "major7": [0, 4, 7, 11], "sus2": [0, 2, 7], "sus4": [0, 5, 7], "dim": [0, 3, 6], "aug": [0, 4, 8], } SCALE_INTERVALS = { "minor": [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10], "major": [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11], "minor7": [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10], "major7": [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11], "sus2": [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11], "sus4": [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11], "dim": [0, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11], "aug": [0, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11], } PENTA = {"minor": [0,3,5,7,10], "major": [0,2,4,7,9]} if mode == "chord": intervals = INTERVALS.get(chord_type, [0,3,7]) elif mode == "scale": intervals = SCALE_INTERVALS.get(chord_type, [0,2,3,5,7,8,10]) elif mode == "penta": intervals = PENTA.get("minor" if "minor" in chord_type else "major", [0,3,5,7,10]) else: intervals = INTERVALS.get(chord_type, [0,3,7]) # Calculate key positions on canvas w = canvas.winfo_width() or 900 h = 180 label_w = 90 white_keys = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 19, 21, 23] n_white = 14 key_w = (w - label_w - 20) / n_white # Map each interval to canvas position COLORS = [GOLD_LT, TEAL, PURPLE, ACCENT, BLUE, GREEN, "#9060d0", GOLD_LT, TEAL, PURPLE] stop_flag = [False] self.pc_anim_stop = stop_flag def highlight_note(note_idx, note: x1 = label_w + wi * key_w + 2 x2 = x1 + key_w - 4 # Highlight rect_id = canvas.create_rectangle(x1, 12, x2, h-22, fill=color, outline=color, tags="anim") name_id = canvas.create_text(x1 + (x2-x1)/2, 12 + (h-34)//2, text=NOTE_NAMES[note], font=("Courier New",13,"bold"), fill="#0a0a0a", tags="anim") if callback: canvas.after(400, callback) return # Black key black_pos = {1:0, 3:1, 6:3, 8:4, 10:5, 13:7, 15:8, 18:10, 20:11, 22:12} for semitone, wi in black_pos.items(): if semitone % 12 == note: x1 = label_w + (wi + 0.65) * key_w x2 = x1 + key_w * 0.7 bh = 12 + (h-32)*0.62 canvas.create_rectangle(x1, 12, x2, bh, fill=color, outline=color, tags="anim") canvas.create_text(x1 + (x2-x1)/2, (12+bh)//2, text=NOTE_NAMES[note], font=("Courier New",8,"bold"), fill="#ffffff", tags="anim") if callback: canvas.after(400, callback) return if callback: canvas.after(100, callback) def animate_sequence(idx=0): if stop_flag[0] or idx >= len(intervals): # Show all together at the end canvas.after(200, lambda: show_all_together()) return canvas.delete("anim") color = COLORS[idx % len(COLORS)] def next_note(): animate_sequence(idx + 1) highlight_note(idx, color, next_note) def canvas.create_text(x1+(x2-x1)/2, 12 + (h-34)//2, text=NOTE_NAMES[note], font=("Courier New",13,"bold"), fill="#0a0a0a", tags="anim") break # Stop any previous animation canvas.delete("anim") animate_sequence(0) def _update_piano_coach(self, canvas, txt): """Draw piano keyboard and generate chord/scale info.""" key = self.pc_key.get() chord_type = self.pc_type.get() mode = that lazy, behind-the-beat feel Velocity: Random variation ±15% — human imperfection Reverb: Plate 0.6s, 20% wet — puts it in a room Tape sat: 10% — adds warmth and vintage character Tip: Slightly OUT the main ones Why: Creates groove and human feel in the pattern How: Set velocity to 20-35% — they should be inaudible but you FEEL the difference when they're removed Simple groove without ghost: 1 - 2 - 3 - 4 - With ghost notes: 1 e 2 e 3 e 4 e The "e" hits are the ghost notes — barely there ── SIDECHAIN FROM SNARE ────────────────────────────── When the snare hits, hi-hat ducks slightly Attack: 1ms · Release: 30ms · Ratio: 2:1 This creates natural space and prevents frequency clash ── RIHANNA / POP ───────────────────────────────────── Volume: -6 to -8dB below snare — present but not harsh note, very consistent velocity Open HH: On the "and" of beat 2 — short and tight Ghost HH: Minimal — pop is cleaner than R&B Velocity: 85-95% consistent — pop is polished, not loose Reverb: Very tight (remove subsonic rumble) Comp: Ratio 3:1 · Attack 8-12ms · Release 60ms Max 3dB GR — punchy and controlled Character: Shorter sustain than Beyoncé — tighter and pop More present in mix — clearly audible Sidechain bass release 60ms — tighter than R&B Beyoncé vs Rihanna kick: Beyoncé = warmer, more emotional, slightly back in mix Rihanna = tighter, poppier, more present, more click ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ This is the stuff top producers do that nobody writes tutorials about. Exact positions, exact timings — not just concepts. At 128 BPM: 1 bar = 1875ms · 1 beat = 469ms · 1/8 = 234ms · 1/16 = 117ms (scale these to your own BPM: 60000/BPM = 1 beat in ms) ── 1. HI-HAT DROP-OUT ──────────────────────────────── Where: Cut the hi-hat layer starting exactly on beat 1 of the LAST bar before the drop — not beat 3, not "somewhere near the end" Length: 1 full bar (4 beats) for a big drop, half a bar (2 beats) for a smaller transition Why: Beat 1 is where the ear expects continuity most — breaking it there is what creates the pull Hear it: Afrobeats/pop build-ups (Tems/Rihanna style) — hi-hat loop stops dead exactly on bar -1, beat 1 ── 2. STILLNESS AS A LAYER (Negative Space) ────────── Where: Cut the element on the "and" of beat 4 in the bar before the drop (the upbeat right before the downbeat) Length: 150-250ms of true silence (roughly a 1/8 to dotted-1/8 note at most tempos) — longer than 300ms starts to feel like a mistake, not a choice Why: 150-250ms is long enough to register consciously but short enough to still feel intentional Hear it: Big EDM drops (Avicii-style) — everything cuts on the last 8th note, even the kick ── 3. RISER AUTOMATION (non-linear) ────────────────── Curve: Exponential (power curve, not linear) — roughly 20% of the rise happens in the first 75% of the time, and 80% of the rise happens in the last 25% Length: 4-8 bars total, but the audible "explosion" part is only the last 500-800ms Why: Matches how real tension/adrenaline builds — slow-slow-slow-FAST, not a steady ramp Hear it: White-noise sweep in house/EDM — near-silent for the first 3s of a 4s riser, explodes in the last 1s ── 4. FILTER SWEEP + NOISE RISER COMBO ─────────────── Where: Start the high-pass sweep on the pad 8 bars out; start the separate noise riser only in the LAST 2 bars, so they converge and peak together Range: HP filter sweeps from ~200Hz up to 8-10kHz over those 8 bars Why: Staggering the start times (not starting both at once) makes the convergence at the drop feel bigger Hear it: Big-room/house build-ups — pad brightens gradually, noise layer only becomes audible in the final 2 bars ── 5. REVERSE CYMBAL / REVERSE FX ──────────────────── Where: Sample length should exactly fill 1 bar (or 2 for a longer build), ending precisely on beat 1 of the drop — the swell peaks exactly on the downbeat Why: A reverse-swell that ends early or late breaks the illusion — timing to the sample must be exact, not just "close enough" Hear it: Nearly every pop/EDM drop — reverse crash timed to land its peak exactly on the drop's beat 1 ── 6. SIDECHAIN AS ARRANGEMENT TOOL (not just bass) ── Settings: Attack 0-5ms, Release 80-120ms, only 2-3dB of gain reduction on pads/arps/vocal chops (kick sidechain on bass is usually 4-8dB — this is subtler) Why: 2-3dB is below conscious detection but still tightens the pocket — more than that and it starts pumping audibly, which isn't the goal here Hear it: Modern house/pop — subtle duck on pads with every kick, separate from and lighter than the bass duck ── 7. PRE-DROP VOLUME DIP ──────────────────────────── Where: Automate a dip on the master bus starting ~150ms before beat 1 of the drop, bottoming out right at the beat, recovering within 50-80ms after Amount: 1-1.5dB — enough to register, not enough to sound like a mistake or a mix error Why: A dip right before a peak makes the peak read as louder than it measures — contrast over volume Hear it: Mastering engineers automate this on the master fader — a few hundred ms dip, then full drop impact ── 8. PITCH AUTOMATION ON LEADS/RISERS ─────────────── Range: +20 to +50 cents (well under a semitone — a full semitone reads as an obvious pitch bend, not tension) Length: Over the last 2-4 bars before the moment of impact Why: Microtonal rise reads as tension to the brain without sounding "out of tune" or gimmicky Hear it: Trap/hip-hop — 808 slides or lead melodies creeping upward right before a beat switch-up ── 9. DELAY-THROW ON THE LAST HIT ──────────────────── Timing: Delay time set to a dotted-1/8 note (roughly 280-350ms at 120-140 BPM) synced to tempo, 2-3 repeats, feedback decaying to silence by the drop Why: Fills exactly the silence window from technique #2 with a decaying tail instead of dead air Hear it: R&B and trap — final clap gets a dotted-1/8 delay-throw fading out right before the drop ── 10. FREQUENCY CARVING BETWEEN LAYERS ────────────── Where: Start the EQ dip automation 200-400ms before the new element's first hit — not simultaneous with it Amount: -2 to -3dB, narrow-ish Q (around 1.5-2), centered on the new element's dominant frequency range Why: Carving the space slightly BEFORE the element arrives (not exactly on it) means the ear already has room ready when the new sound lands Hear it: Before a lead vocal entry — guitar/synth ducked 2-4kHz starting just before the vocal actually hits ── 11. MICRO-TIMING PUSH (the real insider secret) ─── What: Nudge the snare/clap 5-10ms AHEAD of the grid in the final bar before the drop (not behind — ahead) Why: Pushing slightly ahead of the beat creates urgency/rushing feel without the listener consciously clocking it as being "off" — this is what separates polished amateur from pro-level feel Hear it: Top-tier pop/EDM producers do this specifically in the last bar of a build — most producers never touch micro-timing at all, which is exactly why this is a real differentiator ── 12. THE FALSE DROP (fakeout) ────────────────────── What: Build all the way to what sounds like beat 1 of the drop, but only play a single hit (often just the kick or a hit + immediate silence), then do a SECOND, shorter build (1-2 bars) before the real drop lands Why: Resets listener expectation once — the real drop hits harder because the first "drop" primed and then denied the release Hear it: Used sparingly in EDM/pop when producers want an extra-dramatic moment — overuse kills the effect, most tracks should use this once per song at most ── 13. MONO-IZING BEFORE THE DROP ──────────────────── Where: Narrow the stereo width of pads/risers to near-mono in the final 1-2 bars, then snap back to full width exactly on the drop Why: Mono content translates as more "compressed" and tense; the sudden stereo width return on the drop creates an additional sense of "opening up" Hear it: Big-room house/EDM — width automation on the master or on riser buses, tightening into the drop ── 14. SWELLING PAD + GROWING REVERB ───────────────── Where: Start the pad 8 bars before the drop, held on a single sustained chord (the V or a suspended voicing works best — avoid resolving to the I) Filter: High-pass sweep from 300Hz up to 2-3kHz over the full 8 bars — this is what makes it feel like it's "rising" even though the pitch itself never moves Reverb: Automate the wet/dry mix from ~15% at bar -8 up to 60-70% by bar -1 — decay time itself can stay fixed around 3-4s, it's the WET AMOUNT that should grow, not the decay length Volume: Gentle volume swell alongside the filter, +3 to +4dB total across the 8 bars — subtle, the filter and reverb are doing most of the perceived "growth" Why: Growing reverb (not just volume) makes the sound feel like it's physically expanding to fill a bigger room — pairs naturally with technique #3 (riser) without masking it, since they occupy different textural space (tonal pad vs. white noise) Hear it: Cinematic trailers and big pop/EDM builds — a held chord that seems to "bloom" and fill more space the closer you get to the drop, then cuts clean on beat 1 ── 15. DECOUPLED PARAMETER LAYERING (advanced) ─────── What: Instead of automating filter, volume, reverb, and width all on the SAME curve/timeline (which is what most producers do — everything rises together and it reads as one predictable sweep), stagger each parameter on its own independent curve with a different start point, length, and shape Example for an 8-bar cinematic build: • Filter cutoff: exponential curve, bars -8 to -1 • Reverb wet: linear curve, bars -6 to -1 (starts 2 bars LATER than the filter) • Volume swell: logarithmic curve, bars -8 to -2 (ENDS 1 bar EARLIER than the others) • Stereo width: exponential, bars -4 to -1 only (the shortest window — width change reads as more of a "final push" if it's compressed into the least amount of time) Why: When every parameter moves in lockstep, the ear perceives ONE event (a generic "swell"). When each parameter has its own timeline and curve shape, the ear perceives a complex, evolving texture — this is the actual technical difference between a build that sounds "AI-generated/templated" and one that sounds composed by a person with real production experience For sync: Music supervisors and editors specifically listen for this kind of layered complexity — a build that's too uniform reads as "stock music," which is exactly the reputation you don't want when submitting for trailer/sync placement Hear it: High-end trailer music (Two Steps From Hell style, Hans Zimmer-adjacent hybrid scores) — nothing moves in a straight, single curve; everything is staggered ── 16. MULTI-LAYER TRANSIENT STACKING ──────────────── What: Instead of one big impact/hit sound, layer 3-4 DIFFERENT hit sources (e.g. a sub-boom, a metallic clang, a orchestral hit, a distorted kick) with each one offset by a few milliseconds rather than triggered at the exact same sample-accurate instant Timing: Stagger each layer's onset by 5-15ms relative to the "anchor" layer (usually the sub-boom hits first, then the mid/metallic layer 5-8ms later, then any high-frequency transient/crack layer 10-15ms after that) — never all four at 0ms simultaneously EQ: Carve each layer to occupy mostly its own frequency range before stacking — sub-boom owns 30-100Hz, the metallic layer owns 800Hz-4kHz, the crack/transient layer owns 4kHz+ — overlapping ranges get a -2 to -3dB cut on whichever layer is secondary in that band Why: Simultaneous (0ms) layering of multiple full-range sounds causes phase cancellation and a mushy, less powerful result than the sum of its parts. Staggering by a few ms avoids phase issues AND mimics how a real physical impact actually happens — different materials resonate at slightly different speeds, so a "real" impact is never perfectly simultaneous either Hear it: Any high-budget trailer hit — it sounds like ONE massive impact, but it's actually 3-5 layered and staggered sounds working together, not one sample ── 17. OCTAVE-DOUBLED PADS WITHOUT MUD ─────────────── What: Layer the same pad patch one octave down (or up) underneath the main voicing for extra weight/size, without it turning into a muddy low-end mess EQ: On the lower-octave layer specifically: high-pass at 150-200Hz (removes the sub content that would clash with your bass/808), then a broad -3 to -4dB cut around 250-500Hz (the "mud zone" where doubled low-mid content stacks up fastest) Balance: Keep the doubled layer 4-6dB quieter than the main pad in the mix — it should be felt more than heard, reinforcing without announcing itself as a separate element Why: Most producers double an octave down and just turn the fader up until it "sounds bigger," which is what creates boxy, undefined low-mid buildup. Filtering the doubled layer FIRST, then balancing quiet, gives you the size without the mud Hear it: Big cinematic pad walls — full and wide, but the low end stays clean enough for dialogue/SFX to sit on top without a mix engineer needing to carve it out ── 18. HUMANIZED AUTOMATION CURVES ─────────────────── What: Most producers draw one perfectly smooth automation curve (filter sweep, volume swell, etc.) — a single clean exponential or linear line from A to B. Add a small amount of randomized micro-variation ON TOP of that curve so it doesn't read as machine-drawn How: After drawing your main curve, add breakpoints every 200-400ms and nudge each one randomly by ±2-4% of the curve's total range — small enough that the overall shape/direction is unchanged, large enough to remove the "too perfect" quality Why: A perfectly smooth curve is actually what makes a lot of builds sound templated or AI-generated at a subconscious level — real human automation (drawn by hand, or performed on a fader in real time) always has tiny natural irregularities. This technique fakes that human imperfection deliberately For sync: This is one of the more reliable ways to make a build stop sounding "stock" without changing the actual arrangement — supervisors hear hundreds of submissions and the too-smooth ones blur together Hear it: Compare a preset "riser" plugin (very smooth, very clean) to a hand-automated filter sweep in a released trailer track — the hand-automated one has audible "grain" to the movement, even though both are rising ── 19. FREQUENCY-DEPENDENT STEREO PLACEMENT ────────── What: Instead of panning a whole sound to one stereo position, split it into 2-3 frequency bands (e.g. via multiband tools) and place EACH band at a slightly different stereo position Example: On a wide pad or riser — lows (below 200Hz) stay dead center/mono, mids (200Hz-2kHz) panned to about 30-40% width, highs (above 2kHz) panned to full 80-100% width Why: Real acoustic spaces naturally do this — low frequencies are non-directional to human hearing (this is why subwoofers can be placed almost anywhere in a room), while high frequencies are highly directional. Panning a sound's full frequency range identically ignores this, and sounds noticeably more "synthetic" than frequency-dependent placement Why it matters for size: This technique is a major reason certain pads/risers feel "3-dimensional" and huge in professional trailer mixes, versus feeling flat and two-dimensional even when panned wide in a basic way Hear it: High-end cinematic mixes — the low end of a riser feels anchored and centered while the top end feels like it's filling the entire width of the room ── 20. VOCAL CHOP PITCH-MAPPING ─────────────────────── What: Chop a single vocal sample (a word, a syllable, an "ah") into short segments, then re-pitch different chops to different scale degrees so they form a melodic line — effectively turning a vocal sample into a played instrument How: Map each chop to a different key/pad, tuned in semitone steps to match your chord progression — keep chops under 300-400ms so the pitch-shift artifacts read as "stylized" rather than broken Why: A single re-pitched vocal chop played melodically carries emotional weight that a synth can't easily replicate, while staying fully rhythmic/percussive in character — bridges the gap between vocal and instrumental elements For sync: Common in modern trailer and pop-adjacent cinematic work — instantly recognizable "human" texture without needing a full vocal performance or lyrics (useful when you need something vocal-flavored but can't clear/license actual sung lyrics for a sync pitch) Hear it: Modern trailer trailers and pop-leaning cinematic cues — short "ha," "oh," or "ah" hits that follow the melody line rather than just being one static pitch ── 21. DYNAMIC EQ DUCKING (frequency-domain sidechain) ─ What: Instead of ducking an element's VOLUME when another element plays (standard sidechain), duck a SPECIFIC FREQUENCY RANGE only, using a dynamic EQ triggered by the competing element Example: A pad and a lead both have energy around 1-2kHz. Set a dynamic EQ on the pad, sidechained to the lead, cutting -3 to -4dB specifically at 1-2kHz only when the lead is playing — the rest of the pad's frequency range stays untouched Why: Standard volume-sidechain ducks the ENTIRE element, even the frequencies that aren't actually competing — this loses unnecessary energy. Frequency-specific ducking only removes the exact clashing range, so the pad stays present and full everywhere except where it would actually mask the lead Why it's advanced: Most producers don't know their DAW's dynamic EQ can be sidechained this way — it requires understanding exactly which frequencies are competing, not just "turn something down when something else plays" Hear it: Dense modern mixes (pop, hybrid trailer scores) where many elements coexist without ever sounding cluttered or requiring the mix to be sparse to stay clear ── 22. AUTOMATED MODULATION DEPTH (not just rate) ──── What: Most producers automate an LFO's RATE (how fast it wobbles) but leave the DEPTH (how much it wobbles) fixed. Automating the depth itself — starting at 0% and growing over a build — creates a completely different kind of movement Where: On a filter cutoff LFO: start depth at 0% at bar -8, grow to 100% depth by bar -1 — the modulation itself is what "arrives," not just gets faster Why: Rate automation alone still has a constant intensity of movement, just sped up or slowed down. Depth automation makes the movement itself feel like it's being born — nothing wobbles at all until suddenly it does, which reads as tension building differently than a rate change does Hear it: Modern EDM/hybrid builds — a pad that's perfectly still and stable for the first few bars, then starts subtly wobbling, with the wobble growing more extreme as the build progresses, rather than wobbling the whole time at a changing speed ── 23. GRANULAR TIME-STRETCHING FOR TEXTURE BEDS ───── What: Take a very short sample (0.5-2 seconds — a single orchestral note, a vocal fragment, a field recording) and stretch it via granular synthesis into a long, evolving ambient texture (10-30+ seconds) Settings: Grain size 40-100ms, with randomized grain position and slight pitch jitter (±5-10 cents) per grain — this is what prevents the stretched result from sounding like an obvious frozen/looped artifact Why: A granular-stretched texture retains the original sound's harmonic character (still recognizably "that instrument" or "that voice") while becoming something completely new texturally — an entire evolving bed from a single short source, no separate pad synth needed For sync: This is how a lot of modern trailer "atmosphere" beds are actually built — not a synth pad at all, but a tiny fragment of something (often orchestral or vocal) stretched into an ambient wash underneath everything else Hear it: Any cinematic cue with a constantly shifting, slightly grainy ambient texture underneath the main elements — that's very often a granular-stretched source ── 24. SPECTRAL MORPHING BETWEEN TWO SOUNDS ────────── What: Instead of a simple volume crossfade between two sounds (A fades out while B fades in), morph the actual TIMBRE from one to the other using an intermediate blended state — for example, filtering out A's high end while filtering IN B's high end on a different, staggered timeline, rather than a single linear crossfade of both in lockstep Where: Over a 2-4 bar transition: A's low end fades out first (bars 1-2), A's high end fades out last (bars 3-4). B's low end fades in first (bars 1-2), B's high end fades in last (bars 3-4) — same staggering principle as technique #15, applied specifically to a transition between two different sources Why: A straight crossfade of two full-range sounds passes through a "muddy middle" where both are at 50% volume and just sound like an unclear blend. Staggering by frequency band means there's never a point where both sources are competing in the SAME frequency range at full strength simultaneously Hear it: High-end transitions in trailer music — one section's texture seems to dissolve INTO the next one's, rather than one simply fading while the other fades in ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ 🎼 COMPOSER-LEVEL SECRETS (harmony & orchestration) ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ This is the layer most producers never touch — because it's not a plugin or an automation lane, it's a harmony and arrangement decision. This is what separates people who make beats from people who write music. ── 14. THE UNRESOLVED CHORD (harmonic tension) ─────── What: End the build-up on a suspended (sus2/sus4) or add9 chord instead of resolving to the root — hold it through the entire last bar Why: The ear NEEDS resolution once it hears a sus chord. Denying it for 1-2 bars creates tension no amount of volume or noise riser can match Hear it: Cinematic/emotional builds — the pad holds a sus4 right up to the drop, which then resolves to the root exactly on beat 1 ── 15. PEDAL TONE UNDER THE BUILD ──────────────────── What: Hold a single low note (the root, usually) sustained under the entire build-up while the harmony above it changes/moves Why: The ear tracks the fixed pedal note as an anchor, which makes the moving harmony above it feel more unstable and tense by contrast Hear it: Orchestral/cinematic builds (film score technique) — a sustained low string note under shifting chords ── 16. RELATIVE MINOR DROP (mode mixture) ──────────── What: Write the build-up in a major key, then drop into the relative minor (or vice versa) exactly at impact Why: A sudden mode shift is felt before it's consciously understood — it reads as an emotional turn, not just a volume change Hear it: Used in emotional pop/EDM crossovers when a track wants the drop to feel heavier than just "louder" ── 17. RHYTHMIC DISPLACEMENT (used sparingly) ──────── What: Shift the drop's main rhythmic hook to land ONE beat earlier or later than the listener expects based on the build-up's pattern Why: Breaks the listener's predictive pattern-matching for exactly one bar — creates a jolt of surprise distinct from volume/intensity tricks Hear it: Rare but used by top electronic composers when a drop needs to feel "different" from every other drop in the genre — overuse ruins the effect ── 18. VOICE LEADING INTO THE DROP CHORD ───────────── What: Make sure the last note of your build-up melody moves by the smallest possible interval (a half-step or whole-step) into the first note of the drop's main hook/chord Why: Smooth voice leading makes a harmonic transition feel inevitable and connected, even when the underlying chord change is dramatic Hear it: Classical composition principle, borrowed into pop/EDM topline writing — the ear barely notices the mechanics, just that it "flows" ── 19. ORCHESTRATION THINNING (less before more) ───── What: Actively REMOVE 1-2 instruments/layers from the arrangement in the final bar before the drop — not just automate volume down, physically mute Why: A drop that adds elements back on top of a full arrangement has nowhere to go. Thinning first gives the drop somewhere to expand INTO Hear it: Film scores and orchestral EDM crossovers — strip to just percussion + bass right before the full arrangement crashes back in ── 20. THE ANTICIPATION NOTE (composer's pickup) ───── What: Add a single short note or chord stab exactly 1/16 note BEFORE the downbeat of the drop — arriving fractionally early, not on the grid Why: This is a classical "pickup note" device — it gives the ear a head start into the downbeat, making the arrival feel propulsive instead of just loud Hear it: Used constantly in film scoring and increasingly in pop production — most electronic producers never learn this because it's a composition technique, not a DAW technique ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ ⌨️ LOGIC PRO WORKFLOW — Shortcuts That Matter Here ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Default key commands (Logic Pro, macOS). Choose which global track lanes show NAVIGATION (for precise drop timing): Z ................. Zoom to fit selected region(s) Cmd + Left/Right .. Zoom horizontally Cmd + Up/Down ..... Zoom vertically < and > ........... Move playhead back/forward one bar C ................. Cycle mode — loop the selected section (great for looping just the build-up while you dial in automation) ESSENTIALS: Space ............. Play/Stop Q ................. Quantize Cmd + Z ........... Undo X ................. Toggle Mixer view * Ctrl+M is the one most producers never learn — it's the fastest way to execute technique #1 (hi-hat drop-out) without touching automation at all ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ ⌨️ FL STUDIO WORKFLOW — Shortcuts That Matter Here ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Default key commands (FL Studio, Windows — on Mac, Ctrl becomes Cmd and Alt becomes Option). WINDOWS (know these cold): F5 ................ Playlist (arrangement view) F6 ................ Channel Rack (drums/step sequencer) F7 ................ Piano Roll (currently selected channel) F8 ................ Plugin picker F9 ................ Mixer F10 ............... MIDI settings F11 ............... Project info/settings F12 ............... Close all open windows PIANO ROLL TOOLS: B ................. Draw tool E ................. Select/edit tool D ................. Delete tool Ctrl + Q .......... Quick quantize selected notes Alt + Q ........... Open full Quantize settings Ctrl + B .......... Duplicate selected note Ctrl + Shift + 8 .. Move selected notes up an octave (fast way to test melody variations for a riser or lead before the drop) THE ONES ALMOST NOBODY KNOWS: Alt + X ........... Level Scaling — grab and scale ALL selected note velocities/automation at once, instead of adjusting each one by hand. Huge for shaping the volume curve into a build-up fast Alt + R ........... Add random variation to selected notes — instant subtle humanization on hi-hat velocity, useful for the groove techniques we covered earlier Alt + S ...........
