CHAPTERS = { "orchestra": """══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ 🎻 ORCHESTRAL COACH — CHAPTER 1: THE ORCHESTRA ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ The orchestra is a family of instruments working together to create one unified emotional sound. Think of it like a band — but with 60-100 players. ── THE FOUR FAMILIES ───────────────────────────────── 🎻 STRINGS — The emotional heart Violins, Violas, Cellos, Double Bass They carry the melody and the feeling. Most cinematic music starts here. 🎺 BRASS — The power and drama Trumpets, Trombones, French Horns, Tuba They hit you in the chest. Hans Zimmer's signature sound. 🎷 WOODWINDS — The color and texture Flutes, Oboes, Clarinets, Bassoons They add warmth, sadness and magic. Often used for intimate or magical moments. 🥁 PERCUSSION — The pulse and impact Timpani, Snare, Bass Drum, Cymbals, Taiko They create tension, releases and drama. The timpani is the king of cinematic percussion. 👥 CHOIR — The voice of God Soprano, Alto, Tenor, Bass voices They add transcendence and epic scale. Used for the most powerful moments. ── THE ORCHESTRAL REGISTER ────────────────────────── LOW (foundation): Double Bass, Tuba, Bassoon MID-LOW (warmth): Cello, Trombone, Bass Clarinet MID (melody): Viola, French Horn, Clarinet MID-HIGH (presence): Violin, Trumpet, Oboe, Flute HIGH (shimmer/air): Piccolo, High Violin, Triangle RULE: Low instruments = foundation and weight High instruments = melody and emotion Everything in between = harmonic richness ── WHAT MAKES CINEMATIC MUSIC DIFFERENT ───────────── 1. DYNAMIC RANGE — from whisper to explosion The contrast is everything. Quiet makes loud LOUDER. 2. BUILDING — patience is the key Great cinematic music takes time to develop. Don't rush. Let it breathe. 3. SPACE — silence is an instrument The moment before the big hit is as important as the hit itself. 4. LAYERING — one family at a time Start with one instrument → add layers slowly Each new layer must ADD something, not just fill space 5. EMOTION FIRST — technique follows feeling Know WHAT you want people to feel before you decide HOW to create it. ── YOUR TOOLS (what you can use now) ──────────────── FREE: → Spitfire LABS — real orchestral samples, free → BBC Symphony Orchestra Discover — free → Orchestral Companion (iOS/Mac) — affordable PAID: → Omnisphere — incredible cinematic textures + orchestra → EastWest Hollywood Orchestra — film score standard → Spitfire BBC Symphony — professional quality → Cinesamples CineStrings — best strings ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ * You don't need every instrument to start. One great string sound + one great brass sound is enough to begin your first cinematic piece. ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════""", "foundation": """══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ 🎻 ORCHESTRAL COACH — CHAPTER 2: THE FOUNDATION ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Before you place a single note — you need a plan. Cinematic music is architecture. Build the structure first. ── STEP 1: CHOOSE YOUR EMOTION ────────────────────── Everything starts here. What do you want people to FEEL? Epic/Triumphant: → Major key, rising melody, full brass Sad/Melancholic: → Minor key, slow strings, solo instruments Mysterious/Dark: → Phrygian mode, low strings, sparse texture Hopeful: → Major key, slow build, strings + piano Terrifying: → Dissonance, low brass, irregular rhythm Magical/Wonder: → Lydian mode, woodwinds, high strings WRITE THIS DOWN before you open your DAW. ── STEP 2: CHOOSE YOUR KEY ────────────────────────── Most cinematic music is in minor keys — they have more emotional depth than major keys. Best cinematic minor keys: D minor — dark, powerful, dramatic (most used in trailers) C minor — emotional, heavy, intense B minor — mysterious, introspective E minor — heroic sadness, used by John Williams A minor — accessible, emotional, versatile Best cinematic major keys: D major — triumphant, victorious Eb major — grand, noble, royal feel G major — uplifting, adventurous ── STEP 3: CHOOSE YOUR BPM ────────────────────────── Slow (40-70 BPM): Emotional, dramatic, sad scenes Medium (70-100 BPM): Action building, heroic moments Fast (100-140 BPM): Chase scenes, battle music, tension TIP: Many cinematic pieces use HALF TIME feel → Write at 130 BPM but it FEELS like 65 BPM → Gives weight and grandeur to fast passages ── STEP 4: PLAN YOUR ARC ──────────────────────────── Every great cinematic piece has a shape: SIMPLE ARC: Bars 1-8: Quiet intro — solo instrument or pads only Bars 9-16: First layer added — strings enter Bars 17-24: Build — more instruments join Bars 25-32: Pre-climax — brass hints, percussion enters Bars 33-40: CLIMAX — full orchestra, maximum power Bars 41-48: Release — strip back, emotional resolution Bars 49-56: Outro — fade or end on a single note TIP: Resist the urge to go full immediately. The longer you hold back, the bigger the payoff. ── STEP 5: SET UP YOUR DAW ────────────────────────── Create these tracks in order (top to bottom): 1. STRINGS → Violins, Violas, Cellos, Bass 2. BRASS → French Horns, Trumpets, Trombones 3. WOODWINDS → Flutes, Clarinets, Oboes 4. CHOIR → Sopranos, Altos, Tenors, Basses 5. PERCUSSION → Timpani, Taiko, Snare, Cymbals 6. PIANO/HARP → Melodic support 7. SYNTH PADS → Texture and atmosphere (optional) 8. MASTER BUS → Reverb, EQ, compression This layout mirrors the actual orchestra seating. ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ * Don't skip this planning phase. The composers who struggle are those who open their DAW without a clear emotional goal. ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════""", "strings": """══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ 🎻 ORCHESTRAL COACH — CHAPTER 3: STRINGS ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Strings are the heart of the orchestra. Master strings and you can write anything. ── THE STRING FAMILY ───────────────────────────────── VIOLIN (high) — melody and emotion Register: G3 to E7 (sweet spot: D4-A5) Character: Bright, singing, emotional Use for: Main melody, soaring themes VIOLA (mid) — warmth and inner voice Register: C3 to E6 (sweet spot: A3-D5) Character: Darker, warmer than violin Use for: Counter-melody, harmonic filling CELLO (mid-low) — soul and warmth Register: C2 to C6 (sweet spot: G2-G4) Character: Rich, emotional, human-like voice Use for: Bass melody, emotional themes, counterpoint DOUBLE BASS (low) — foundation and weight Register: E1 to G3 (sweet spot: E1-D3) Character: Deep, powerful, dark Use for: Bass line, adding weight to low end ── HOW STRINGS MOVE ───────────────────────────────── LEGATO (smooth, connected): → Long bow strokes, notes overlap → Emotional, singing, flowing → Use for: Slow melodies, pads, emotional themes → In DAW: Long notes, overlapping slightly STACCATO (short, detached): → Short bow strokes, notes separated → Energetic, rhythmic, driving → Use for: Action music, building tension → In DAW: Short notes with gaps between PIZZICATO (plucked): → Finger plucks the string instead of bow → Light, delicate, rhythmic → Use for: Light moments, quirky scenes → Think: counting scenes, light comedy TREMOLO (very fast bow): → Rapid back-and-forth bowing → Tense, nervous, mysterious → Use for: Horror, tension, suspense → In DAW: Use tremolo articulation if available ── WRITING STRINGS STEP BY STEP ───────────────────── STEP 1: Write the cello melody first The cello is the most versatile — start here. Write a simple 4-bar melody in your chosen key. Example in D minor: Bar 1: D3 (1 bar) — the root, grounded Bar 2: F3-A3 (half bar each) — rising Bar 3: C3-E3-G3 (flowing) — building Bar 4: D3 (whole bar) — resolution STEP 2: Add the violin melody above Take the cello melody and move it up an octave. Or write a counter-melody that answers the cello. STEP 3: Add violas in between Fill the harmonic space between cello and violin. Play the chord tones that aren't already covered. STEP 4: Add double bass below Double the cello an octave lower for weight. Or play long sustained root notes. ── STRING VOICING TIPS ─────────────────────────────── Low strings (cello + bass): root and 5th of chord Violas: 3rd and 7th of chord Violins: melody + 5th above melody AVOID: Having all strings in the same octave → They'll clash and sound muddy SPACE THEM OUT like this: Bass: D2 Cello: D3 + A3 Viola: F3 + C4 Violin: A4 + D5 ── VELOCITY = EMOTION ──────────────────────────────── pp (very soft, vel 20-35): Intimate, fragile, far away p (soft, vel 35-55): Warm, gentle, inner voice mp (medium, vel 55-70): Natural, present, warm mf (medium loud, vel 70-85): Confident, present, clear f (loud, vel 85-95): Powerful, emotional peak ff (very loud, vel 95-110): Maximum drama, climax TIP: Vary the velocity slightly even within one section → Real string sections are never robotically even → ±5-10 velocity variation makes it feel human ── OMNISPHERE STRINGS ──────────────────────────────── Search in Omnisphere browser: → "strings ensemble" for full section sound → "cello solo" for intimate close sound → "string pad" for atmospheric texture Attack: 80-200ms for legato feel Release: 600ms-1s for natural tail Reverb: Hall, 2-3s decay, 25% wet — place them in a hall ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ * Start with just cello + violin. Two well-written string parts sound more powerful than four mediocre ones. ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════""", "brass": """══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ 🎻 ORCHESTRAL COACH — CHAPTER 4: BRASS ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Brass is the power of the orchestra. When brass enters — people feel it in their chest. This is the Hans Zimmer signature sound. ── THE BRASS FAMILY ────────────────────────────────── FRENCH HORN (mid) — warm, heroic, epic Register: B1 to F5 (sweet spot: F2-C4) Character: Round, warm, heroic, noble Use for: Heroic themes, emotional swells, hunting calls Hans Zimmer uses: Massive french horn swells TRUMPET (high) — bright, heroic, fanfare Register: F#3 to D6 (sweet spot: G3-C5) Character: Bright, piercing, triumphant Use for: Fanfares, victories, dramatic announcements TROMBONE (mid-low) — powerful, dark, noble Register: E1 to Bb4 (sweet spot: Bb1-F3) Character: Bold, powerful, dark when low Use for: Dark moments, power, low brass chords TUBA (low) — foundation, dark power Register: D1 to F3 (sweet spot: D1-Bb2) Character: Massive, dark, ominous Use for: Deep bass foundation, villain themes ── HOW BRASS ENTERS ───────────────────────────────── The biggest mistake: Brass too early and too loud. RULE: Brass enters AFTER the strings have established the emotional world. They arrive to amplify — not replace. Timeline of a cinematic build: Bar 1-8: Strings only — establish the emotion Bar 9-12: French horn hint — a single note or two Bar 13-16: Trombones add weight below strings Bar 17-20: Full brass joins — EXPLOSION of sound When brass arrives LATE — it feels like a reward. When brass arrives EARLY — it feels ordinary. ── WRITING BRASS STEP BY STEP ─────────────────────── STEP 1: French Horn sustain Start with a single long French Horn note. The 5th of the chord is always safe. D minor chord → French Horn holds A2 (the 5th) STEP 2: Add trombone below Trombone plays the root note an octave lower. D minor chord → Trombone holds D1 (root, low) STEP 3: Add trumpets above Trumpets double the string melody an octave higher. Or they play a fanfare-style figure above. STEP 4: Full brass chord Stack the chord across all brass instruments: Tuba: D1 (root, very low) Trombone: D2-F2 (root + 3rd) French Horn: A2-D3 (5th + octave) Trumpet: F3-A3 (3rd + 5th, high) ── THE HANS ZIMMER BRASS SOUND ────────────────────── Hans Zimmer's signature: → MASSIVE French Horn swells — dozens layered → Low trombone foundation that you FEEL not hear → Brass hits on unexpected beats — not always beat 1 → Brass + low string unison = maximum impact How to recreate in your DAW: → Layer 3-4 French Horn tracks, slightly detuned → Add long attack (300ms) — they swell in slowly → Hard compression to even out the dynamics → Large hall reverb 3-4s decay → Boost 150-200Hz for chest-punch low brass feel ── BRASS ARTICULATIONS ─────────────────────────────── LONG/SUSTAIN: Powerful, swelling, emotional → Attack 200-400ms, long decay → Use for: Swells, emotional peaks SHORT/STACCATO: Impact, punchy, dramatic → Attack 10ms, release 200ms → Use for: Hits, accents, action SFORZANDO (sudden loud): Shock, impact, surprise → Sudden loud note then immediate soft → Use for: Jump scares, dramatic revelations ── OMNISPHERE BRASS ────────────────────────────────── Search: "brass ensemble", "french horn", "trombone" Or use: "cinematic brass" for pre-made patches Settings: Attack: 200-400ms (swelling, not instant) Release: 800ms-1.5s Reverb: Large hall, 3-4s decay, 35% wet Eq: Boost +2dB at 150Hz for chest punch ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ * Less is more with brass. One perfectly placed French Horn note is more powerful than 10 poorly placed trumpet blasts. ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════""", "woodwinds": """══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ 🎻 ORCHESTRAL COACH — CHAPTER 5: WOODWINDS ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Woodwinds add COLOR to the orchestra. They fill the space between strings and brass and give the music personality and texture. ── THE WOODWIND FAMILY ─────────────────────────────── FLUTE (high) — magical, airy, innocent Register: C4 to C7 (sweet spot: D4-A6) Character: Light, bright, magical, innocent Use for: Magical scenes, birds, nature, delicate moments Famous: Hedwig's Theme (Harry Potter) — solo flute OBOE (mid-high) — plaintive, pastoral, emotional Register: Bb3 to A6 (sweet spot: C4-G5) Character: Nasal, penetrating, emotional, pastoral Use for: Sad solos, nature scenes, emotional solos Famous: Used in almost every sad cinematic moment CLARINET (mid) — warm, versatile, lyrical Register: E3 to C7 (sweet spot: G3-C6) Character: Warm in low register, bright in high Use for: Lyrical melodies, warm inner voice, jazz fusion Famous: Schindler's List — solo clarinet + violin BASSOON (low) — dark, quirky, comic or ominous Register: Bb1 to Eb5 (sweet spot: C2-G4) Character: Dark, rich, slightly comic or sinister Use for: Dark underscoring, comic moments, bass support ── HOW WOODWINDS WORK IN FILM MUSIC ───────────────── Woodwinds rarely play the main melody in climax. They are most powerful in QUIET moments. QUIET moments: Woodwind solo = maximum emotional impact LOUD moments: Woodwinds add color above brass and strings The oboe solo in a quiet scene hits harder than a full brass chord in a loud one. Use them wisely — don't bury them. ── WRITING WOODWINDS ───────────────────────────────── STEP 1: The flute counter-melody While strings play the main melody, add a light flute figure above: → Short phrases of 4-8 notes → Move in contrary motion to the melody → Stay in the upper register (D5-A6) STEP 2: Oboe for emotional moments In the quiet sections — give the oboe a solo. The oboe sounds mournful and human — like a voice. → Legato, slow-moving melody → Let it breathe — don't fill every beat STEP 3: Clarinets for warmth Clarinets double the violas an octave up. This adds warmth and presence to the middle register. STEP 4: Bassoon for darkness In dark or mysterious sections: → Bassoon doubles the cello melody → Or plays a slow chromatic descent below the strings → Adds weight and unease ── ICONIC WOODWIND MOMENTS IN CINEMA ──────────────── Schindler's List: Solo violin + clarinet = heartbreak Harry Potter: Solo flute = magic and wonder Star Wars: Oboe in "Force Theme" = nostalgia Inception: Slow low woodwind = dread and weight Up (Married Life): Strings + woodwinds = joy then sadness ── WOODWIND VOICING WITH STRINGS ──────────────────── The best combinations: Flute + Violin: Bright, soaring, magical Oboe + Viola: Warm, melancholic, intimate Clarinet + Cello: Rich, lyrical, romantic Bassoon + Bass: Dark, heavy, ominous AVOID: Woodwind + same-register brass → They clash and the woodwind disappears ── OMNISPHERE WOODWINDS ───────────────────────────── Search: "flute solo", "oboe", "clarinet", "woodwind" Settings for realism: Attack: 40-80ms (breath takes time to engage) Release: 200-400ms Vibrato: Delayed onset 200ms, depth 4 cents Reverb: Small hall, 1-1.5s, 18% wet ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ * The oboe is the most underrated cinematic instrument. A solo oboe line in a quiet moment will make people feel more than a full orchestral climax. ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════""", "percussion": """══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ 🎻 ORCHESTRAL COACH — CHAPTER 6: PERCUSSION ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Percussion is the physical force of the orchestra. It creates tension, announces drama and releases energy. Without percussion — cinematic music has no pulse. ── THE PERCUSSION FAMILY ───────────────────────────── TIMPANI (kettle drums) — the king of cinematic percussion Pitch: Tunable — usually set to root or 5th of key Character: Deep, resonant, ominous, powerful Use for: Building tension, dramatic announcements, climax TAIKO DRUMS — massive impact, Japanese power Character: Booming, primitive, earth-shaking Use for: Battle scenes, epic climax, tribal energy Hans Zimmer: Used heavily in Inception, Dark Knight SNARE DRUM — rhythmic tension, military feel Character: Sharp, driving, military precision Use for: Action sequences, marching, building energy BASS DRUM — ultimate impact Character: Booming, powerful, the biggest hit Use for: The biggest moments, final impacts CYMBALS — shimmer, crash, release Crash cymbal: For dramatic impacts Suspended cymbal (swell): Building tension Hi-hats: Light rhythmic texture GONG — doom, ceremony, epic scale Character: Massive, resonant, ancient Use for: The most dramatic moments, endings ── THE TIMPANI IS EVERYTHING ──────────────────────── In cinematic music, timpani = drama. Every great trailer uses timpani rolls. TUNE THE TIMPANI to your key: D minor → Timpani on D2 and A2 (root and 5th) C minor → Timpani on C2 and G2 ROLLS (sustained tremolo): → Start soft → crescendo → release → Creates maximum tension before a hit → The longer the roll — the bigger the payoff SINGLE HITS: → On unexpected beats for maximum shock → Not always on beat 1 — try beat 2 or 4 → The space before the hit is the tension ── WRITING PERCUSSION STEP BY STEP ────────────────── STEP 1: Timpani foundation Place a long timpani roll starting 4 bars before climax. Start at velocity 30 → end at velocity 110. Hit the root note on the first beat of the climax. STEP 2: Bass drum on impact Layer a single bass drum hit with the timpani climax hit. The bass drum adds the physical impact your body feels. STEP 3: Cymbal crash Add a crash cymbal on the same climax beat. It adds the shimmer and release after the impact. STEP 4: Taiko drums for building In the 8 bars before climax: → Taiko hits on beats 2 and 4 → Gradually increase velocity → Add more hits as you approach the climax STEP 5: Snare for action sections In action or building sections: → Snare roll under the strings → Creates urgency and forward motion ── THE PERCUSSION PLACEMENT RULE ──────────────────── BEFORE the climax: Percussion builds (timpani roll) ON the climax: Percussion hits everything at once AFTER the climax: Percussion fades out slowly NEVER hit everything at once from bar 1. The hit only works if there was silence before it. ── ICONIC PERCUSSION MOMENTS ──────────────────────── Inception (Time): Single piano + slow percussion = dread Dark Knight (Why So Serious): Low brass + irregular percussion Gladiator (Now We Are Free): Taiko + strings = ancient epic Avengers Theme: Snare march + brass + timpani Star Wars (Imperial): Timpani + brass hits = evil power ── DAW SETTINGS FOR ORCHESTRAL PERCUSSION ─────────── Timpani: → Long attack (softer hits) or instant (hard hits) → Reverb: Large hall 3-4s — it needs to RING → Tune to your key's root or 5th Taiko: → Fast attack, long decay → Reverb: Huge room or outdoor reverb → Boost 80-120Hz for maximum chest punch Cymbal crash: → Instant attack, very long decay (let it ring) → High-pass at 400Hz — only shimmer, no boom ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ * The timpani roll before the climax is the most powerful tool in cinematic music. Practice building a 4-bar roll that peaks at the exact right moment. ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════""", "choir": """══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ 🎻 ORCHESTRAL COACH — CHAPTER 7: CHOIR ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ The choir is the voice of the divine. When choir enters — everything becomes transcendent. It's the most powerful tool in cinematic music. ── THE CHOIR SECTIONS ──────────────────────────────── SOPRANO (very high female voices) Register: C4 to C6 Character: Angelic, pure, soaring, otherworldly Use for: Highest emotional peaks, angelic moments ALTO (lower female voices) Register: F3 to F5 Character: Warm, rich, emotional, grounded Use for: Harmonic support, emotional depth TENOR (high male voices) Register: C3 to C5 Character: Heroic, powerful, noble Use for: Heroic moments, male power themes BASS (low male voices) Register: E2 to E4 Character: Deep, authoritative, dark, God-like Use for: Dark power, villains, ancient themes ── WHAT MAKES CHOIR SO POWERFUL ───────────────────── 1. The human voice triggers the most emotional response Our brains are wired to respond to voices. 2. Choir sounds timeless — it could be ancient or future Unlike synths or guitars, choir has no "era" 3. Mass of voices = transcendence One voice = human. Hundred voices = divine. 4. Wordless choir (aahs and oohs) is most cinematic Words attach to meaning — wordless attaches to feeling ── TYPES OF CHOIR WRITING ─────────────────────────── AAH/OOH CHOIR (most common in film): → Long sustained notes → Very slow movement, mostly staying on one note → Perfect for: Backgrounds, emotional swells Example in D minor: Soprano: A4 (long, 2 bars) Alto: F4 (long, 2 bars) Tenor: D3 (long, 2 bars) Bass: D2 (long, 2 bars) → This creates a rich D minor chord that SWELLS SYLLABIC CHOIR (rhythmic, each syllable = note): → More energetic, driving → "Dun dun dun" style → Perfect for: Action, villains, menacing themes → Example: O Fortuna (Carmina Burana) MELISMATIC CHOIR (one syllable over many notes): → Flowing, melodic, angelic → One long "aaahhh" over a melody → Perfect for: Angelic moments, endings, wonder ── WRITING CHOIR STEP BY STEP ─────────────────────── STEP 1: Hold the chord Don't move yet. Let all four choir sections hold a simple chord for 2 full bars. D minor: Bass D2, Tenor D3, Alto F4, Soprano A4 STEP 2: Move the soprano After 2 bars, move just the soprano up by a step. D minor: Soprano moves from A4 to C5 Everything else stays. The soprano leads. STEP 3: Resolve to the root After 2 more bars, move soprano back down to A4. This creates a simple but emotional motion. STEP 4: Add a swell Use a volume automation curve: Bar 1: start soft (velocity 30) Bar 2: grow slowly Bar 3: peak (velocity 90) Bar 4: hold or fade STEP 5: Add the orchestra underneath Strings sustain the same chord below the choir. Choir + strings = transcendent wall of sound. ── WHEN TO BRING IN THE CHOIR ─────────────────────── RULE: Choir comes in AFTER the climax has built. It is the REWARD at the top of the mountain. Build: Strings → Brass → Percussion Climax: All three together Transcendence: Choir enters above everything else The choir should feel like the emotional ceiling has been broken through. Like something greater than human has arrived. ── OMNISPHERE CHOIR ────────────────────────────────── Search: "choir", "voices", "aah", "ooh" Settings: Attack: 400-800ms (voices swell slowly) Release: 1-2s (they fade naturally) Vibrato: Delayed 400ms, depth 6 cents Reverb: Cathedral or large hall, 4-6s decay, 35% wet Width: 90-100% — choir should be very wide Omnisphere Harmonia: Add +5th at -8dB and +octave at -12dB → Creates the illusion of many more voice layers ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ * The choir works best when it arrives unexpectedly. If the listener is waiting for it — it loses power. Bring it in one bar earlier or later than expected. ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════""", "arc": """══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ 🎻 ORCHESTRAL COACH — CHAPTER 8: BUILD THE ARC ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ This is where everything comes together. A complete cinematic piece — from silence to explosion and back to silence. ── THE COMPLETE ORCHESTRAL ARC ────────────────────── We're building a 64-bar cinematic piece in D minor. This is the blueprint. Adapt it to your own vision. ── BARS 1-8: THE SEED ──────────────────────────────── Instrumentation: Solo cello OR solo piano only Dynamic: pp (very soft, velocity 25-40) Character: Lonely, intimate, searching What to play: → Simple 4-note melody in D minor → D3 — F3 — A3 — C3 (slow, one note per bar) → Long notes, no rhythm yet → No percussion, no brass, no choir Reverb: Large hall — make it sound distant and alone THE GOAL: Make the listener lean in and listen. Silence + one instrument = curiosity. ── BARS 9-16: FIRST LIFE ───────────────────────────── Add: Viola joins the cello Dynamic: p (soft, velocity 40-55) What to add: → Viola plays a counter-melody below the cello → Move in opposite direction to cello → Still very quiet — just two voices talking ALSO: Add a very quiet timpani pedal point → Single low D1 held for 4 bars, very soft → It's barely there — just felt, not heard ── BARS 17-24: THE WORLD OPENS ────────────────────── Add: Full string section enters Dynamic: mp (medium soft, velocity 55-70) What to add: → Violins take the melody from the cello → Cello moves to bass support role → Viola fills the harmonic middle → Double bass enters with long low notes ALSO: French Horn enters — single sustained note → A2 (the 5th of D minor) — very soft → It's just a hint of brass to come ── BARS 25-32: TENSION BUILDS ─────────────────────── Add: Brass hint + woodwinds + percussion building Dynamic: mf (medium loud, velocity 70-80) What to add: → Oboe counter-melody above strings → French Horns swell louder → Timpani begins a slow roll (D2) → Taiko drums — single hits on beats 2 and 4 THIS IS THE PRE-CLIMAX ZONE. Everything is building but hasn't exploded yet. Hold back. Make them wait. ── BARS 33-40: THE EXPLOSION ───────────────────────── ADD EVERYTHING. This is the climax. Dynamic: ff (very loud, velocity 95-110) What happens: → Full string section at maximum velocity → Full brass: Trumpets, Trombones, French Horns, Tuba → Timpani HARD HIT on bar 33 beat 1 → Bass drum on bar 33 beat 1 → Crash cymbal on bar 33 beat 1 → Taiko drums driving the rhythm → CHOIR enters — aahs on D minor chord → Woodwinds add color above brass The simultaneous timpani + bass drum + cymbal on bar 33 beat 1 is the moment everything releases. ── BARS 41-48: THE RELEASE ─────────────────────────── Start removing layers — reverse the build Dynamic: f down to mp (velocity 85 down to 60) What to remove: → Percussion stops (except timpani fade) → Brass becomes quiet — sustain only → Choir fades slowly → Strings carry the emotion alone again ── BARS 49-56: REFLECTION ──────────────────────────── Back to small forces — but transformed Dynamic: p (soft, velocity 40-55) What to play: → Strings only — same melody from bar 1 → But now it feels DIFFERENT — earned, changed → Cello takes melody again → Viola and violin provide quiet support ── BARS 57-64: THE ENDING ──────────────────────────── Options for ending: TRAGIC ENDING: Land on D minor chord and hold. Fade out slowly over 4 bars. HOPEFUL ENDING: Resolve to D MAJOR on the last bar. This unexpected major chord = hope after darkness. UNRESOLVED ENDING: Stop on the 7th chord (C major). Leave the listener hanging — perfect for trailers. ── THE LAYERING SCHEDULE ──────────────────────────── Bars 1-8: Solo cello/piano only Bars 9-16: + Viola + Timpani pedal Bars 17-24: + Full strings + French Horn hint Bars 25-32: + Woodwinds + Full brass hint + Percussion building Bars 33-40: + EVERYTHING + Choir Bars 41-48: - Percussion - Most brass - Choir fading Bars 49-56: - Back to strings only Bars 57-64: - Final resolution ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ * Follow this blueprint for your first piece. Then break the rules and make it your own. ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════""", "mix": """══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ 🎻 ORCHESTRAL COACH — CHAPTER 9: MIX IT ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Mixing orchestral music is different from pop mixing. The goal is NOT loudness — the goal is SPACE and DEPTH. You want to place instruments in a virtual concert hall. ── THE ORCHESTRAL MIX PHILOSOPHY ──────────────────── Pop mixing: Everything forward, loud, in your face Orchestral mixing: Depth, distance, perspective Think of it like a concert hall: Front/close: Solo instruments, important melodies Mid distance: String sections, main ensemble Far back: Brass, Percussion (they naturally project) Sides: Wide elements, choir Above/behind: Reverb tail, atmosphere ── EQ FOR EACH INSTRUMENT GROUP ───────────────────── STRINGS: High-pass: 40Hz (remove sub rumble) Cut: -1dB at 300Hz (reduce boxiness) Boost: +1dB at 3-5kHz (presence, detail) Air: +0.5dB at 12kHz (shimmer) BRASS: High-pass: 50Hz Boost: +2dB at 150Hz (chest punch, warmth) Cut: -1.5dB at 600Hz (horn honk) Presence: +1dB at 4kHz WOODWINDS: High-pass: 150Hz (remove low rumble) Presence: +1.5dB at 3-4kHz (cut through strings) Air: +1dB at 10kHz CHOIR: High-pass: 100Hz Cut: -2dB at 300-500Hz (reduce boxy chest resonance) Presence: +1dB at 3kHz (clarity for words/vowels) Air: +1dB at 12kHz TIMPANI: Tune carefully to your key Boost: +3dB at 80-100Hz (the boom) Cut: -2dB at 400Hz (remove cardboard sound) Transient: fast attack, long release ── REVERB — THE MOST IMPORTANT ELEMENT ───────────── Orchestral music LIVES in reverb. Without reverb — it sounds like samples in a box. With the right reverb — it sounds like a real orchestra. REVERB TYPE: Hall reverb (always) → Simulate a concert hall or church DIFFERENT REVERB SIZES PER INSTRUMENT: Solo instruments: Short reverb 1-1.5s (closer to listener) String sections: Medium reverb 2-2.5s Brass sections: Long reverb 3-3.5s (they sit further back) Choir: Very long reverb 4-5s (they're at the back) Timpani: Cathedral reverb 3-4s (let it ring and ring) USE PRE-DELAY: Solo instruments: pre-delay 10-15ms (brings forward) Section instruments: pre-delay 20-30ms Brass/Choir: pre-delay 30-50ms (pushes further back) Valhalla Reverb or Altiverb are ideal. Valhalla Supermassive (FREE) works excellently. ── COMPRESSION — USE VERY LITTLE ──────────────────── Unlike pop music — orchestral music needs DYNAMICS. The soft parts must be soft. The loud parts LOUD. That contrast IS the emotion. Strings: 1.5:1 ratio max, slow attack (50ms), slow release Brass: 2:1 max, medium attack (20ms) Percussion: NO compression — let the transients breathe Choir: 2:1 max, slow attack (30ms) NEVER use heavy limiting on cinematic music. Target: -18 to -20 LUFS — leave the dynamics alive. ── PANNING — MIRROR THE REAL ORCHESTRA ────────────── Real orchestral seating (from conductor's perspective): Far Left: First Violins Left: Second Violins, Violas Center: Cellos, Conductor, Solo instruments Right: Double Bass, Bassoon Far Right: French Horns, Trumpets Back Left: Trombones, Tuba Back Right: Timpani, Percussion Wide: Choir (spread across the whole back) In your DAW: Violin 1: Pan L40-60 Violin 2: Pan L20-40 Viola: Pan L10-20 Cello: Pan CENTER to slight R Bass: Pan CENTER French Horn: Pan R20-40 Trumpet: Pan R30-50 Choir: Width 90-100% ── MASTER BUS SETTINGS ─────────────────────────────── Use: 🎨 Vibe Settings → 🏔 Epic/Orchestral in MCS Target: -18 to -20 LUFS integrated LRA: 12-18 LU — maximum dynamic range True Peak: -3dBTP — leave headroom for sync/film mix ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ * The mix is finished when you close your eyes and believe you're sitting in a concert hall. If you still hear "samples" — add more reverb. ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════""", "styles": """══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ 🎻 ORCHESTRAL COACH — CHAPTER 10: STYLES ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Different cinematic contexts need different approaches. It's to give the\n" out += " limiter LESS work to do in the first place.\n\n" out += "── 1. CLIP GAIN — DO THIS FIRST ──────────────────────\n\n" out += " Before any plugin, manually pull down the loudest\n" out += " individual peaks in your DAW (clip gain / region gain).\n" out += " → Target: reduce the 3-5 loudest spikes by -2 to -4 dB\n" out += " → This removes 'fake' peaks that don't represent\n" out += " the actual energy of the track\n" out += " → Result: the limiter barely needs to touch anything\n\n" out += "── 2. PARALLEL COMPRESSION ───────────────────────────\n\n" out += " Send the full mix to a parallel bus:\n" out += " → Heavy compression: ratio 8:1, fast attack, fast release\n" out += " → Gain reduction: 10-15 dB on this bus\n" out += " → Blend in at 10-20% under the dry mix\n" out += " → This adds perceived loudness and density WITHOUT\n" out += " compressing the main signal's transients\n" out += " → Tool: any compressor — even a free one works\n\n" out += "── 3. MULTIBAND COMPRESSION ──────────────────────────\n\n" out += " Only compress the bands that need it:\n" out += " → Low band (20-200Hz): gentle, 1.5:1, controls bass swell\n" out += " → Mid band (200Hz-4kHz): usually leave alone — this is\n" out += " where dynamics live, don't touch unless there's a problem\n" out += " → High band (4kHz+): gentle, catches harsh peaks only\n" out += " → Tool: FabFilter Pro-MB or Ozone Dynamics\n" out += " → Max 1-2 dB GR per band — this is surgical, not heavy\n\n" out += "── 4. SATURATION FOR PERCEIVED LOUDNESS ──────────────\n\n" out += " Saturation adds harmonics that make a track FEEL\n" out += " louder without raising the actual peak level:\n" out += " → Tape saturation: 10-20% drive across the whole mix\n" out += " → Tool: Softube Tape, Slate VTM, Decapitator\n" out += " → This is one of the most underused loudness tricks\n\n" out += "── 5. THE GLUE COMPRESSOR ────────────────────────────\n\n" out += " One gentle bus compressor to tie everything together:\n" out += " → Ratio 2:1 · Attack 30ms · Release auto/100ms\n" out += " → Max 1.5-2 dB gain reduction — barely visible\n" out += " → Tool: SSL G-Bus style, or Pro-MB single band\n\n" out += "── 6. THE LIMITER — LAST RESORT, NOT THE WORKHORSE ───\n\n" out += " By this point your peaks should already be controlled.\n" out += " The limiter should now only catch occasional spikes:\n" out += " → True Peak ceiling: -1 dBTP (streaming) or -0.3 (club)\n" out += " → Gain reduction should rarely exceed 1-2 dB\n" out += " → If you're seeing 4-6+ dB constant reduction —\n" out += " go back to steps 1-5, you're relying on the\n" out += " limiter to do work it shouldn't be doing\n" out += " → Tool: FabFilter Pro-L2, transparent mode\n\n" out += "── 7. CHECK THE RESULT ───────────────────────────────\n\n" out += " → A/B against a reference track at matched loudness\n" out += " → Check LRA (Loudness Range) — should still be\n" out += " 3-6 LU for most genres. Below 2 LU = over-compressed\n" out += " → Listen for transients: do drums still 'punch'?\n" out += " → If everything sounds flat and tiring — you went\n" out += " too far. Loud should still feel exciting, not exhausting\n\n" out += "══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" out += " THE CORE PRINCIPLE:\n" out += " Loudness = many small, smart gain reductions spread\n" out += " across the chain — NOT one big limiter doing\n" out += " everything at the end.\n\n" out += " * Trust your ears — these are starting points\n" out += "══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" txt.config(state="normal") txt.delete("1.0", tk.END) txt.insert("1.0", out) txt.config(state="disabled") def _show_soft_warm(self): """Open Soft & Warm Master guide in apart venster — tegenhanger van Loud but Dynamic.""" win = tk.Toplevel(self) win.title("🌙 Soft & Warm Master — MCS") win.geometry("820x720") win.configure(bg=BG) win.resizable(True, True) hdr = tk.Frame(win, bg=BG, pady=12) hdr.pack(fill="x", padx=20) tk.Frame(hdr, bg=PURPLE, width=3).pack(side="left", fill="y", padx=(0,10)) title_f = tk.Frame(hdr, bg=BG); Wide LRA (6-12 LU).\n" out += " This is the opposite philosophy of 'Loud but Dynamic' —\n" out += " here, space and softness ARE the goal, not a side effect.\n\n" out += "── 1. GAIN STAGING — LEAVE ROOM TO BREATHE ───────────\n\n" out += " Don't push your mix bus hot. Aim for peaks around\n" out += " -6 to -10 dBFS before any processing.\n" out += " → This headroom is what lets the master stay soft\n" out += " → No need for clip gain or peak-shaving here —\n" out += " a soft master doesn't fight its own peaks\n\n" out += "── 2. GENTLE EQ — SUBTRACT, DON'T BOOST ──────────────\n\n" out += " Warmth comes from removing harshness, not adding bass:\n" out += " → High-pass at 30-40Hz to clean the sub without\n" out += " removing warmth\n" out += " → Gentle cut -1 to -2dB around 2-4kHz if anything\n" out += " feels 'edgy' or fatiguing\n" out += " → Optional: a soft high-shelf cut above 12kHz,\n" out += " -0.5 to -1dB, rolls off digital harshness\n" out += " → Tool: FabFilter Pro-Q3, wide soft-knee bells\n\n" out += "── 3. ANALOG-STYLE SATURATION — THE WARMTH ENGINE ────\n\n" out += " This is the heart of a warm master:\n" out += " → Tape saturation: 15-30% drive — more than the\n" out += " Loud but Dynamic recipe, since here it's the\n" out += " main character, not a support tool\n" out += " → Tube/valve saturation on top for extra harmonics\n" out += " → Tool: Softube Tape, Slate VTM, Waves J37,\n" out += " or a tube preamp plugin (Kazrog, UAD 610)\n" out += " → Listen for: rounder transients, smoother highs\n\n" out += "── 4. SLOW, GENTLE COMPRESSION ────────────────────────\n\n" out += " Compression here should be felt, not heard:\n" out += " → Ratio 1.5:1 to 2:1\n" out += " → Attack: slow, 30-50ms — let transients through\n" out += " → Release: slow, 200-400ms or auto — breathing, not pumping\n" out += " → Max 1-1.5 dB gain reduction\n" out += " → Tool: an opto-style compressor (LA-2A style) —\n" out += " their natural slow behavior fits this perfectly\n\n" out += "── 5. STEREO WIDTH — WIDE BUT NATURAL ─────────────────\n\n" out += " → Widen mid-to-high content gently (110-120%)\n" out += " → Keep bass and vocals centered and mono below 150Hz\n" out += " → A subtle stereo reverb send (10-15%) on the\n" out += " whole mix bus adds cohesion and air\n" out += " → Tool: Ozone Imager, or a simple M/S EQ widen\n\n" out += "── 6. NO HARD LIMITING ────────────────────────────────\n\n" out += " This is the biggest difference from a loud master:\n" out += " → True Peak ceiling: -1.5 to -2 dBTP — more headroom\n" out += " than a typical streaming master\n" out += " → Gain reduction on the limiter: 0.5 dB or less —\n" out += " it should almost never engage\n" out += " → If the limiter is doing real work, you pushed\n" out += " too hot upstream — go back and lower gain staging\n" out += " → Tool: FabFilter Pro-L2 in 'transparent' mode,\n" out += " or skip the limiter entirely and just trim gain\n\n" out += "── 7. THE FINAL CHECK ──────────────────────────────────\n" out += " → LUFS integrated should land -16 to -20\n" out += " → LRA should be wide — 6-12 LU is healthy here\n" out += " (a narrow LRA means you've accidentally squashed it)\n" out += " → Listen on headphones at low volume — does it\n" out += " still feel full and warm, or thin and empty?\n" out += " → A/B against a reference like a Bon Iver, Phoebe\n" out += " Bridgers or ambient/lo-fi reference track\n\n" out += "── WHEN TO USE THIS VS LOUD BUT DYNAMIC ───────────────\n" out += " Soft & Warm → lo-fi, ambient, acoustic, ballads,\n" out += " ASMR/meditation, ASMR sync, ASMR style content,\n" out += " intimate vocal tracks, Spotify/streaming where\n" out += " loudness normalization makes extra loudness pointless\n" out += " Loud but Dynamic → trailers, action sync, energetic\n" out += " pop, hip-hop, EDM, anywhere impact and presence\n" out += " need to compete in a loud playback environment\n\n" out += "══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" out += " THE CORE PRINCIPLE:\n" out += " Headroom is the feature, not the problem.\n" out += " Let the track breathe — that space IS the warmth.\n\n" out += " * Trust your ears — these are starting points\n" out += "══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" txt.config(state="normal") txt.delete("1.0", tk.END) txt.insert("1.0", out) txt.config(state="disabled") def _show_vocal_warmth(self): """Open Vocal Warmth Guide in apart venster.""" win = tk.Toplevel(self) win.title("🎤 Vocal Warmth Guide — MCS") win.geometry("820x720") win.configure(bg=BG) win.resizable(True, True) # Header hdr = tk.Frame(win, bg=BG, pady=12) hdr.pack(fill="x", padx=20) tk.Frame(hdr, bg=ACCENT, width=3).pack(side="left", fill="y", padx=(0,10)) title_f = tk.Frame(hdr, bg=BG); text = self.ma_entry.get().strip() chords = text.upper().split() if not chords: return NOTE_SEMI = {"C":0,"C#":1,"DB":1,"D":2,"D#":3,"EB":3,"E":4, "F":5,"F#":6,"GB":6,"G":7,"G#":8,"AB":8,"A":9,"A#":10,"BB":10,"B":11} CHORD_TYPES = { "M":"Majeur","MIN":"Mineur","":"Majeur (impliciet)", "7":"Dominant 7","MAJ7":"Majeur 7","M7":"Mineur 7", "DIM":"Verminderd","AUG":"Vergroot","SUS2":"Sus2","SUS4":"Sus4", } MOOD_MAP = { ("Am","F","C","G"): "Emotioneel, nostalgisch — meest gebruikte pop progressie", ("Dm","Bb","F","C"): "Donker, dramatisch — cinematic minor", ("C","G","Am","F"): "Positief, melodisch — universele pop", ("Am","G","F","G"): "Rock, agressief, voortstuwend", ("Am","F","C","E"): "Cinematisch, mysterieus — minor met majeur V", ("Cm","Ab","Eb","Bb"):"Donker, episch — veel in cinematic", } import re parsed = [] for chord in chords: m = re.match(r"([A-G][B#]?)(M7|MAJ7|MIN|DIM|AUG|SUS2|SUS4|M|7|)", chord) if m: root, quality = m.group(1), m.group(2) semi = NOTE_SEMI.get(root.replace("B","BB") if root.endswith("B") and len(root)>1 else root, 0) parsed.append({"chord":chord,"root":root,"quality":quality,"semi":semi}) if not parsed: return # Bepaal toonsoort roots = [n["semi"] for n in parsed] MAJOR_KEY_CHORDS = { 0:["C","Dm","Em","F","G","Am","Bdim"], 2:["D","Em","F#m","G","A","Bm","C#dim"], 4:["E","F#m","G#m","A","B","C#m","D#dim"], 5:["F","Gm","Am","Bb","C","Dm","Edim"], 7:["G","Am","Bm","C","D","Em","F#dim"], 9:["A","Bm","C#m","D","E","F#m","G#dim"], 11:["B","C#m","D#m","E","F#","G#m","A#dim"], } NOTE_NAMES = ["C","C#","D","Eb","E","F","F#","G","Ab","A","Bb","B"] # Vind meest waarschijnlijke toonsoort best_key = 0; best_score = -1 for key_semi, key_chords in MAJOR_KEY_CHORDS.items(): score = sum(1 for n in parsed if any(n["root"] in c or c.startswith(n["root"]) for c in key_chords)) if score > best_score: best_score = score; best_key = key_semi key_name = NOTE_NAMES[best_key] chord_tuple = tuple(c["chord"] for c in parsed) mood = MOOD_MAP.get(chord_tuple, "Analyze by feel — every progression has unique energy") # Genereer variaties VARIATIONS = [ "Voeg een 7de toe: " + " ".join(c["chord"]+"7" for c in parsed), "Omkering (swap 1 en 3): " + " ".join([parsed[2]["chord"],parsed[1]["chord"], parsed[0]["chord"],parsed[3]["chord"]] if len(parsed)>=4 else [c["chord"] for c in parsed]), "Minor parallel: " + " ".join(c["chord"]+"m" if not c["quality"] else c["chord"] for c in parsed), ] # Sync genre suggesties op basis van progressie has_minor = any("M" not in p["quality"] and p["root"]+"m" in ["Am","Dm","Em","Gm","Cm","Fm","Bm","Bbm"] for p in parsed) sync_genres = (["Emotional drama","Cinematic sad","Dark thriller"] if has_minor else ["Uplifting corporate","Happy pop","Inspirational"]) out = f"── CHORD ANALYSIS ───────────────────────────────\n" out += f" Progressie: {text}\n" out += f" Key: {key_name} ({'mineur' if has_minor else 'majeur'})\n" out += f" Sfeer: {mood}\n\n" out += f"── CHORD DETAILS ────────────────────────────────\n" for c in parsed: qt = CHORD_TYPES.get(c["quality"], c["quality"]) out += f" {c['chord']:<8} {c['root']} {qt}\n" out += f"\n── VARIATIES ─────────────────────────────────────\n" for v in VARIATIONS: out += f" → {v}\n" out += f"\n── SYNC GENRE SUGGESTIES ─────────────────────────\n" for sg in sync_genres: out += f" ✓ {sg}\n" out += f"\n── GEBRUIK IN SYNC ───────────────────────────────\n" tips = [ "Play each chord for 2 beats for a 4/4 feel", "Vertraag naar 1 akkoord per maat voor meer spanning", "Gebruik als basis voor de hoofdmelodie", f"Combineer met BPM 70-90 voor {('emotionele' if has_minor else 'positieve')} sync tracks", ] for t in tips: out += f" → {t}\n" self._write(self.ma_txt, out) # ── VIDEO SYNC TOOL ─────────────────────────────────── def _build_video_sync(self, parent): # Wrapped in a scrollable canvas — this screen has maximum energy and intensity" cut_times = beat_times[::1] # Limit to first 60 cuts for readability cut_times = cut_times[:60] self.vid_status.config(text=f"✅ {len(cut_times)} edit points generated · "#1a3a3a", "#3a1a1a"] # Draw shots between cuts prev_x = 20 for i, ct in enumerate(cut_times): x = 20 + (float(ct) / max_t) * (w - 40) color = shot_colors[i % len(shot_colors)] # Shot rectangle sb_canvas.create_rectangle(prev_x, 20, x-1, 90, fill=color, outline="#e8c04033") # Shot number mid_x = (prev_x + x) / 2 shot_w = x - prev_x if shot_w > 25: sb_canvas.create_text(mid_x, 55, text=str(i+1), font=("Courier New",8,"bold"), fill="#e8c04088") # Cut line sb_canvas.create_line(x, 15, x, 95, fill="#e8c040", width=1) # Time label mins = int(float(ct) // 60) secs = float(ct) % 60 if i % max(1, len(cut_times)//12) == 0: sb_canvas.create_text(x, 105, text=f"{mins}:{secs:04.1f}", font=("Courier New",7), fill="#4a6a8a", anchor="center") prev_x = x # Last shot if len(cut_times) > _auto_beat_markers(self): """Auto detect beats from music and place as sync markers.""" if not self.vid_mus_file: messagebox.showwarning("No music", "Choose a music file first.") return self.vid_status.config(text="⏳ Detecting beats..."); self.update() try: import librosa, numpy as np y, sr = librosa.load(self.vid_mus_file, sr=None, mono=True, duration=180) tempo, beat_frames = librosa.beat.beat_track(y=y, sr=sr) beat_times = librosa.frames_to_time(beat_frames, sr=sr) # Only take every 4th beat (every bar) to avoid too many markers bar_times = beat_times[::4] self.sync_markers = [] for i, t in enumerate(bar_times): mins = int(t // 60) secs = t % 60 self.sync_markers.append({ "num": i + 1, "time": float(t), "timestamp": f"{mins:02d}:{secs:05.2f}", "label": f"Bar {i+1} ({float(np.atleast_1d(tempo)[0]):.0f} BPM)" }) self._update_timeline() self._update_markers_txt() self.vid_status.config( text=f"✅ {len(self.sync_markers)} bar markers detected · {float(np.atleast_1d(tempo)[0]):.0f} BPM · every 4 beats") except ImportError: self.vid_status.config(text="❌ librosa required — already included in MCS") except Exception as e: self.vid_status.config(text=f"❌ {str(e)[:80]}") def _analyse_scene_mood(self): """Analyse the music mood for sync placement suggestions.""" if not self.vid_mus_file: messagebox.showwarning("No music", "Choose a music file first.") return self.scene_mood_lbl.config(text="⏳ Analysing..."); self.update() try: import librosa, numpy as np y, sr = librosa.load(self.vid_mus_file, sr=None, mono=True, duration=90) duration = librosa.get_duration(y=y, sr=sr) tempo, _ = librosa.beat.beat_track(y=y, sr=sr) rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(y**2))) lufs = round(20 * np.log10(rms + 1e-10) + 3, 1) S = np.abs(librosa.stft(y, n_fft=2048)) freqs = librosa.fft_frequencies(sr=sr, n_fft=2048) avg = np.mean(S, axis=1) total = np.sum(avg) + 1e-10 def bp(lo, hi): m = (freqs >= lo) & (freqs < hi) return float(np.sum(avg[m]) / total * 100) low_e = bp(20, 250) mid_e = bp(250, 4000) high_e = bp(4000, 20000) # Determine mood bpm = float(np.atleast_1d(tempo)[0]) if bpm < 80 and low_e > 40: mood = "Dark / Cinematic" scenes = "• Night scenes · Emotional moments · Loss · Reflection" color = "#6040a0" elif bpm < 80: mood = "Emotional / Intimate" scenes = "• Close-up moments · Romance · Sad scenes · Nature" color = "#4080c0" elif bpm < 110 and mid_e > 40: mood = "Warm / Soulful" scenes = "• Character development · Relationships · Everyday life" color = "#c08030" elif bpm < 110: mood = "Uplifting / Hopeful" scenes = "• Success moments · New beginnings · Travel · Achievement" color = "#40a060" elif bpm < 140 and low_e > 35: mood = "Energetic / Powerful" scenes = "• Action sequences · Sports · Chase scenes · Drama" color = "#e87030" else: mood = "Intense / Driving" scenes = "• Fast action · Climax scenes · Tension · Confrontation" color = "#e83040" result = ( f"🎭 {mood} · {bpm:.0f} BPM · {lufs:.1f} LUFS\n" f"Best for: {scenes}" ) # Show detailed popup win = tk.Toplevel(self) win.title("🎭 Scene Mood Analysis") win.geometry("680x400") win.configure(bg=BG) tk.Label(win, text="🎭 SCENE MOOD ANALYSIS", font=F_MED, fg=color, bg=BG).pack(pady=(20,4), padx=20, anchor="w") tk.Frame(win, bg=color, height=2).pack(fill="x", padx=20) info_f = tk.Frame(win, bg=BG2, padx=16, pady=14); info_f.pack(fill="x", padx=20, pady=12) tk.Label(info_f, text=f"Mood: {mood}", font=F_LABEL, fg=color, bg=BG2).pack(anchor="w", pady=2) tk.Label(info_f, text=f"BPM: {bpm:.0f}", font=F_LABEL, fg=FG, bg=BG2).pack(anchor="w", pady=2) tk.Label(info_f, text=f"Loudness: {lufs:.1f} LUFS", font=F_LABEL, fg=FG, bg=BG2).pack(anchor="w", pady=2) tk.Label(info_f, text=f"Low energy: {low_e:.0f}% · Mids: {mid_e:.0f}% · Highs: {high_e:.0f}%", font=F_LABEL, fg=FG2, bg=BG2).pack(anchor="w", pady=2) tk.Label(win, text="BEST FOR THESE SCENES:", font=F_LABEL, fg=FG2, bg=BG).pack(anchor="w", padx=20, pady=(4,2)) for scene in scenes.split("·"): s = scene.strip().replace("•","").strip() if s: tk.Label(win, text=f" → {s}", font=("Courier New",10), fg=color, bg=BG).pack(anchor="w", padx=20) tk.Label(win, text="\nSYNC PLACEMENT TIPS:", font=F_LABEL, fg=FG2, bg=BG).pack(anchor="w", padx=20) tips = { "Dark / Cinematic": ["Use in establishing shots — wide landscape", "Let music play before dialogue starts", "Perfect for title sequences"], "Emotional / Intimate": ["Sync to close-up facial expressions", "Let music swell on the emotional peak", "Avoid cutting during the melody"], "Warm / Soulful": ["Works well under dialogue", "Let it breathe — don't over-edit", "Good for montage sequences"], "Uplifting / Hopeful": ["Sync the drop to a character breakthrough", "Use rising melody for rising action", "Perfect for end credits"], "Energetic / Powerful": ["Sync drum hits to visual cuts", "Music change = scene change", "Use silence before the big moment"], "Intense / Driving": ["Every beat = a cut", "Build to maximum intensity", "End abruptly for maximum impact"], } for tip in tips.get(mood, []): tk.Label(win, text=f" • {tip}", font=("Courier New",9), fg=FG2, bg=BG).pack(anchor="w", padx=20) tk.Button(win, text="✕ Close", font=F_LABEL, bg=BG3, fg=FG2, relief="flat", cursor="hand2", padx=20, pady=6, command=win.destroy).pack(pady=16) self.scene_mood_lbl.config(text=f"🎭 {mood} · {bpm:.0f} BPM", fg=color) except Exception as e: self.scene_mood_lbl.config(text=f"❌ {str(e)[:60]}") def _mark_sync_point(self): """Mark a sync point at the current playback position.""" import datetime if not self.vid_start_time: self.vid_status.config(text="⚠️ Press Play Both first, then mark sync points") return now = datetime.datetime.now() elapsed = (now - self.vid_start_time).total_seconds() mins = int(elapsed // 60) secs = elapsed % 60 timestamp = f"{mins:02d}:{secs:05.2f}" marker_num = len(self.sync_markers) + 1 self.sync_markers.append({ "num": marker_num, "time": elapsed, "timestamp": timestamp, "label": f"Marker {marker_num}" }) self._update_timeline() self._update_markers_txt() self.vid_status.config(text=f"🎯 Marker {marker_num} set at {timestamp}") def _timeline_click(self, event): """Add a marker by clicking on the timeline.""" self._mark_sync_point() def _update_timeline(self): """Draw timeline with sync markers.""" canvas = self.timeline_canvas canvas.delete("all") w = canvas.winfo_width() or 600 h = 60 # Timeline bar canvas.create_rectangle(10, 25, w-10, 35, fill="#1a1a2a", outline="#2a2a4a") # Duration line canvas.create_text(10, 15, text="0:00", font=("Courier New",7), fill="#444", anchor="w") if not self.sync_markers: canvas.create_text(w//2, 42, text="No sync markers yet — press SPACE while playing", font=("Courier New",8), fill="#333", anchor="center") return # Get max time for scaling max_time = max(m["time"] for m in self.sync_markers) + 5 canvas.create_text(w-10, 15, text=f"{int(max_time//60):02d}:{max_time%60:04.1f}", font=("Courier New",7), fill="#444", anchor="e") colors = [ACCENT, TEAL, GOLD_LT, PURPLE, GREEN, "#e870c8"] for i, marker in enumerate(self.sync_markers): x = 10 + (marker["time"] / max_time) * (w - 20) color = colors[i % len(colors)] # Marker line canvas.create_line(x, 10, x, 50, fill=color, width=2) # Marker dot canvas.create_oval(x-5, 22, x+5, 38, fill=color, outline=color) # Number canvas.create_text(x, 55, text=str(marker["num"]), font=("Courier New",7,"bold"), fill=color, anchor="center") def _update_markers_txt(self): """Update the markers text list.""" self.markers_txt.config(state="normal") self.markers_txt.delete("1.0", tk.END) if not self.sync_markers: self.markers_txt.insert("1.0", "No markers yet") else: for m in self.sync_markers: self.markers_txt.insert(tk.END, f" 🎯 Marker {m['num']:2d} → {m['timestamp']} | {m['label']}\n") self.markers_txt.config(state="disabled") def _clear_sync_markers(self): """Clear all sync markers.""" self.sync_markers = [] self._update_timeline() self._update_markers_txt() self.vid_status.config(text="🗑 Markers cleared") def _export_cue_sheet(self): """Export sync markers as a cue sheet.""" if not self.sync_markers: messagebox.showwarning("No markers", "Mark some sync points first.") return fname = os.path.basename(self.vid_file) if self.vid_file else "video" mfname = os.path.basename(self.vid_mus_file) if self.vid_mus_file else "music" out = "══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" out += f" 🎬 CUE SHEET — SYNC MARKERS\n" out += "══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n" out += f" Video: {fname}\n" out += f" Music: {mfname}\n" out += f" Markers: {len(self.sync_markers)}\n\n" out += "── SYNC POINTS ───────────────────────────────────────\n\n" for m in self.sync_markers: out += f" [{m['num']:02d}] {m['timestamp']} → {m['label']}\n" out += "\n══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" out += " * Use these timestamps to align your music\n" out += " with the key moments in your video.\n" out += "══════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" self.clipboard_clear() self.clipboard_append(out) messagebox.showinfo("✅ Exported", "Cue sheet copied to clipboard!\nPaste it in your notes or DAW.") def _editor_preview(self): """Preview video + music together.""" import subprocess if not self.editor_vid_file: messagebox.showwarning("No video", "Load a video first.") return self._editor_stop_preview() # Open the video with QuickTime via the plain `open` command instead of # AppleScript automation — AppleScript requires macOS "Automation" # permission (System c["duration"] safe_text = (c["text"].replace("\\", "") .replace(":", r"\:") .replace("'", r"\'")) drawtext_filters.append( f"drawtext=fontfile={font_path}:text='{safe_text}':" Pattern input pattern_f = tk.Frame(win, bg="#0a0a14", pady=4); pattern_f.pack(fill="x") tk.Label(pattern_f, text="PATTERN (e.g. 2,2,4,8,1,4):", font=("Courier New",8), fg="#e8c040", bg="#0a0a14").pack(side="left", padx=(12,4)) pattern_entry = tk.Entry(pattern_f, font=("Courier New",10), bg=BG3, fg="#e8c040", insertbackground="#e8c040", relief="flat", width=24) pattern_entry.insert(0, "2,2,4,8,2,4") pattern_entry.pack(side="left", padx=(0,8), ipady=3) tk.Label(pattern_f, text="← repeats automatically", font=("Courier New",8), fg=FG3, bg="#0a0a14").pack(side="left") # Info label info_lbl = tk.Label(ctrl, text=f"🎵 {bpm:.0f} BPM · {len(self.auto_image_files)} images · {os.path.basename(self.auto_audio_file)}", font=("Courier New",9), fg="#4a6a9a", bg="#0a0a14") info_lbl.pack(side="right", padx=12) # Image counter counter_lbl = tk.Label(ctrl, text="", font=("Courier New",10,"bold"), fg="#e870c8", bg="#0a0a14") counter_lbl.pack(side="right", padx=(0,12)) # State player_state = {"running": False, "idx": 0, "job": None, "proc": None} images = self.auto_image_files.copy() def load_image(path, w, h): try: img = Image.open(path) img.thumbnail((w, h), Image.LANCZOS) return ImageTk.PhotoImage(img) except Exception: return None def show_image(idx): w = img_canvas.winfo_width() or 780 h = img_canvas.winfo_height() or 520 path = images[idx % len(images)] photo = load_image(path, w, h) if photo: img_canvas.delete("all") img_canvas.create_image(w//2, h//2, image=photo, anchor="center") img_canvas._photo = photo # keep reference counter_lbl.config(text=f"{(idx % len(images))+1} / {len(images)}") # Energy array for energy-based mode hop = 512 rms = librosa.feature.rms(y=y, hop_length=hop)[0] rms_times_arr = librosa.frames_to_time(np.arange(len(rms)), sr=sr, hop_length=hop) rms_max = float(np.max(rms)) + 1e-10 def get_delay(current_time_s): """Get next delay based on variation mode.""" import random mode = var_mode.get() base = int(beat_var.get()) if mode == "fixed": return beat_ms * base elif mode == "random": choices = [1, 2, 2, 4, 4, 8] return beat_ms * random.choice(choices) elif mode == "energy": # Find current RMS energy idx = np.searchsorted(rms_times_arr, current_time_s) idx = min(idx, len(rms)-1) energy = float(rms[idx]) / rms_max # High energy = fast (1-2 beats), low energy = slow (4-8 beats) if energy > 0.7: every = 1 elif energy > 0.4: every = 2 elif energy > 0.2: every = 4 else: every = 8 return beat_ms * every elif mode == "pattern": try: parts = [int(x.strip()) for x in pattern_entry.get().split(",") if x.strip()] if not parts: parts = [2] every = parts[player_state["idx"] % len(parts)] except Exception: every = 2 return beat_ms * every return beat_ms * base pattern_idx = [0] def next_image(): if not player_state["running"]: return player_state["idx"] += 1 show_image(player_state["idx"]) # Calculate current time current_t = player_state["idx"] * (beat_ms / 1000.0) * int(beat_var.get()) delay = get_delay(current_t) player_state["job"] = win.after(int(delay), next_image) def start_player(): import subprocess stop_player() player_state["running"] = True player_state["idx"] = 0 show_image(0) proc = subprocess.Popen(["afplay", self.auto_audio_file]) player_state["proc"] = proc delay = get_delay(0) player_state["job"] = win.after(int(delay), next_image) mode = var_mode.get().upper() info_lbl.config(text=f"▶ Playing · {bpm:.0f} BPM · {mode} mode") def stop_player(): player_state["running"] = False if player_state["job"]: win.after_cancel(player_state["job"]) player_state["job"] = None if player_state["proc"]: try: player_state["proc"].terminate() except: pass player_state["proc"] = None info_lbl.config(text=f"⏹ Stopped · {bpm:.0f} BPM · {len(images)} images") win.protocol("WM_DELETE_WINDOW", lambda: [stop_player(), win.destroy()]) # Show first image win.update() show_image(0) except ImportError: self.auto_status.config(text="❌ PIL required — pip install Pillow") except Exception as e: self.auto_status.config(text=f"❌ {str(e)[:80]}") def _pick_auto_audio(self): path = filedialog.askopenfilename( title="Choose audio", filetypes=[("Audio","*.mp3 *.wav *.flac *.aiff"),("All","*.*")]) if path: self.auto_audio_file = path self.auto_audio_lbl.config( text=f" {os.path.basename(path)}", fg=GOLD_LT) def _pick_auto_images(self): paths = filedialog.askopenfilenames( title="Choose images", filetypes=[("Images","*.jpg *.jpeg *.png *.bmp *.webp"),("All","*.*")]) if paths: self.auto_image_files.extend(list(paths)) self.auto_img_lbl.config( text=f" {len(self.auto_image_files)} images selected", fg=GOLD_LT) def _clear_auto_images(self): self.auto_image_files = [] self.auto_img_lbl.config(text="No images selected", fg=FG2) def _auto_sync(self): if not self.auto_audio_file: messagebox.showwarning("Missing", "Choose an audio file first!") return if not self.auto_image_files: messagebox.showwarning("Missing", "Add images first!") return self.auto_status.config(text="⏳ Analyzing audio and images..."); self.update() try: import librosa, numpy as np from PIL import Image # ── Analyseer audio ─────────────────────────── y, sr = librosa.load(self.auto_audio_file, sr=None, mono=True) duration = librosa.get_duration(y=y, sr=sr) tempo, beats = librosa.beat.beat_track(y=y, sr=sr) bpm = float(np.atleast_1d(tempo)[0]) # Energie per sectie n_sections = len(self.auto_image_files) section_dur = duration / n_sections section_samples = int(section_dur * sr) energies = [] for i in range(n_sections): start = i * section_samples end = min((i+1) * section_samples, len(y)) section = y[start:end] rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(section**2))) energies.append(rms) # Normaliseer energie 0-100 max_e = max(energies) if max(energies) > 0 else 1 norm_energies = [e/max_e*100 for e in energies] # ── Analyseer images ────────────────────────── def analyse_img_quick(path): img = Image.open(path).convert("RGB") img_small = img.resize((50,50)) pixels = np.array(img_small).reshape(-1,3).astype(float) brightness = float(np.mean(pixels)) sat = float(np.std(pixels)) r = float(np.mean(pixels[:,0])) b = float(np.mean(pixels[:,2])) # Energie score van de foto img_energy = (brightness/255*50) + (sat/100*50) dominant = "warm" if r > b+20 else ("cool" if b > r+20 else "neutral") return img_energy, brightness, dominant img_data = [analyse_img_quick(p) for p in self.auto_image_files] # ── Match audio energie aan foto energie ────── # Sorteer foto's op energie score maar respecteer volgorde # Gebruik audio energie om de juiste foto te kiezen # Maak matching: welke foto past bij welk audio moment # Op basis van energie gelijkenis img_energies = [d[0] for d in img_data] # Simpele matching: hoge audio energie = energieke foto matched = [] available = list(range(len(self.auto_image_files))) for audio_e in norm_energies: if not available: break # Vind foto met dichtstbijzijnde energie best_idx = min(available, key=lambda i: abs(img_energies[i] - audio_e)) matched.append(best_idx) available.remove(best_idx) # ── Genereer output ─────────────────────────── MOOD_MAP = [ (80, "Energetic", "Am - Dm - F - E", "Synths + Full Drums"), (60, "Climax", "Dm - Bb - F - C", "Orchestra + Percussion"), (40, "Building", "Am - F - C - G", "Piano + Strings building"), (20, "Calm", "Cmaj7 - Am7 - F - G", "Piano + Soft pads"), (0, "Intro/Outro","Am - F - C - Em", "Piano solo"), ] def get_mood(energy): for threshold, mood, chords, instruments in MOOD_MAP: if energy >= threshold: return mood, chords, instruments return "Minimal", "Am - F", "Piano" out = "══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" out += " 🎵🖼️ AUTO SYNC — COMPLETE TIMELINE\n" out += f" Audio: {os.path.basename(self.auto_audio_file)}\n" out += f" {len(self.auto_image_files)} images · {bpm:.0f} BPM · {duration:.1f} sec total\n" out += "══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n" for i, img_idx in enumerate(matched): start_s = i * section_dur end_s = (i+1) * section_dur start_str = f"{int(start_s//60)}:{int(start_s%60):02d}" end_str = f"{int(end_s//60)}:{int(end_s%60):02d}" audio_e = norm_energies[i] img_e, brightness, dominant = img_data[img_idx] mood, chords, instruments = get_mood(audio_e) fname = os.path.basename(self.auto_image_files[img_idx])[:25] # Energy bar bar_len = int(audio_e / 10) energy_bar = "█" * bar_len + "░" * (10 - bar_len) out += f" [{start_str} → {end_str}] ──────────────────────\n" out += f" Image: {fname}\n" out += f" Audio: [{energy_bar}] {audio_e:.0f}%\n" out += f" Mood: {mood}\n" out += f" Chords: {chords}\n" out += f" Instruments: {instruments}\n" out += f" Color: {'Warm' if dominant=='warm' else 'Cool' if dominant=='cool' else 'Neutral'} · Brightness {brightness:.0f}/255\n\n" out += "── DAW INSTRUCTIONS ──────────────────────────────\n" out += f" 1. Set DAW to {bpm:.0f} BPM\n" out += f" 2. Each section = {section_dur:.1f} seconds\n" out += f" 3. Import images in the order shown above\n" out += f" 4. Match chord changes to section boundaries\n" out += f" 5. Let audio energy guide your arrangement\n\n" out += "── AUTO SYNC TIP ─────────────────────────────────\n" out += " High energy audio + bright image = drop/climax\n" out += " Low energy audio + dark image = intro/outro\n" out += " The app matched images to audio energy automatically\n" out += "══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" self._write(self.vs_txt, out) self.auto_status.config( text=f"✅ {len(matched)} photos synced to audio · {bpm:.0f} BPM · {duration:.1f}s") except Exception as e: import traceback self.auto_status.config(text=f"❌ {str(e)[:60]}") def _pick_video(self): path = filedialog.askopenfilename( title="Choose video", filetypes=[("Video","*.mp4 *.mov *.avi *.mkv"),("Alle","*.*")]) if path: self.vs_file = path self.vs_path_lbl.config(text=f" {os.path.basename(path)}", fg=FG) self.vs_status.config(text="Video loaded — click Analyze Scenes") def _analyse_video(self): if not self.vs_file: messagebox.showwarning("No video","Choose a video file first.") return self.vs_status.config(text="⏳ Analyzing...") self.update() try: import cv2 import numpy as np except ImportError: try: import sys, subprocess self.vs_status.config(text="⏳ Installing opencv...") self.update() subprocess.check_call([ "/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.11/bin/python3.11", "-m","pip","install","opencv-python","--quiet"]) import cv2 import numpy as np except Exception: self.vs_status.config(text="❌ Video analysis requires opencv") self._write(self.vs_txt, "Video scene analysis requires opencv.\n\n" "Install via terminal:\n" " /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.11/bin/python3.11 -m pip install opencv-python\n\n" "The other features (Image → Music, Slideshow Sync, Auto Sync) work without opencv.") return try: cap = cv2.VideoCapture(self.vs_file) fps = cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS) or 25 total_frames = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT)) duration_s = total_frames / fps fname = os.path.basename(self.vs_file) # Analyseer elke 5 seconden een frame segments = [] interval = int(fps * 5) prev_brightness = None for seg_idx in range(0, total_frames, interval): cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES, seg_idx) ret, frame = cap.read() if not ret: break # Analyseer frame gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY) brightness = float(np.mean(gray)) contrast = float(np.std(gray)) hsv = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV) saturation = float(np.mean(hsv[:,:,1])) hue_mean = float(np.mean(hsv[:,:,0])) # Detecteer scène type time_s = seg_idx / fps time_str= f"{int(time_s//60)}:{int(time_s%60):02d}" # Bepaal sfeer op basis van visuele kenmerken if brightness < 60: mood = "Donker / nacht" music = "Dark ambient, tension, minor keys" bpm = "60-90 BPM" elif brightness > 180: mood = "Helder / overdag" music = "Uplifting, corporate, major keys" bpm = "100-130 BPM" elif saturation > 120: mood = "Kleurrijk / energiek" music = "Upbeat, action, pop" bpm = "120-140 BPM" elif saturation < 50: mood = "Desaturated / melankolisch" music = "Emotional, sad, ambient" bpm = "65-85 BPM" else: mood = "Neutraal / drama" music = "Cinematic, emotional, mid-tempo" bpm = "80-110 BPM" # Detecteer cuts (grote brightness verandering) cut_detected = False if prev_brightness is not None: if abs(brightness - prev_brightness) > 40: cut_detected = True prev_brightness = brightness segments.append({ "time": time_str, "brightness": brightness, "contrast": contrast, "mood": mood, "music": music, "bpm": bpm, "cut": cut_detected, }) cap.release() # Output out = f"══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n" out += f" 🎬 VIDEO SYNC ANALYSE\n" out += f" 📁 {fname}\n" out += f" ⏱ Duur: {int(duration_s//60)}:{int(duration_s%60):02d} · {fps:.0f} fps\n" out += f"══════════════════════════════════════════════════\n\n" out += f"── SCÈNE ANALYSE PER 5 SECONDEN ──────────────────\n\n" for seg in segments: cut_marker = " ✂️ SCENE CUT" if seg["cut"] else "" out += f" [{seg['time']}]{cut_marker}\n" out += f" Sfeer: {seg['mood']}\n" out += f" Muziek: {seg['music']}\n" out += f" BPM: {seg['bpm']}\n" out += f" Helderheid: {seg['brightness']:.0f} Contrast: {seg['contrast']:.0f}\n\n" # Algemene aanbevelingen avg_brightness = float(np.mean([s["brightness"] for s in segments])) n_cuts = sum(1 for s in segments if s["cut"]) out += f"── ALGEMENE AANBEVELINGEN ────────────────────────\n" out += f" Gemiddelde helderheid: {avg_brightness:.0f}\n" out += f" Gedetecteerde cuts: ~{n_cuts}\n" if avg_brightness < 100: out += f" → Donkere video — gebruik minor keys, ambient of tension\n" out += f" → Aanbevolen BPM: 60-90\n" elif avg_brightness > 160: out += f" → Heldere video — gebruik major keys, uplifting\n" out += f" → Aanbevolen BPM: 100-130\n" else: out += f" → Gebalanceerde video — cinematic of emotional werkt goed\n" out += f" → Aanbevolen BPM: 80-110\n" if n_cuts > 5: out += f" → Veel cuts — gebruik muziek met duidelijke hits en energie\n" else: out += f" → Weinig cuts — langzame opbouw werkt goed\n" self._write(self.vs_txt, out) self.vs_status.config(text=f"✅ {len(segments)} segmenten geanalyseerd") except Exception as e: librosa.get_duration(y=y, sr=sr) mins = int(dur//60); secs = int(dur%60) # ── BPM detectie ────────────────────────────── tempo1, _ = librosa.beat.beat_track(y=y, sr=sr) bpm1 = float(np.atleast_1d(tempo1)[0]) oenv = librosa.onset.onset_strength(y=y, sr=sr) tempo2 = librosa.feature.tempo(onset_envelope=oenv, sr=sr) bpm2 = float(np.atleast_1d(tempo2)[0]) bpm = float(np.median([bpm1, bpm2])) if bpm > 180: bpm /= 2 if bpm < 55: bpm *= 2 # ── Pitch detectie ──────────────────────────── # Gebruik ZCRT voor ruwe pitch schatting zcr = float(librosa.feature.zero_crossing_rate(y).mean()) chroma = librosa.feature.chroma_cqt(y=y, sr=sr) key_idx = int(np.argmax(chroma.mean(axis=1))) NOTE_NAMES = ["C","C#","D","Eb","E","F","F#","G","Ab","A","Bb","B"] # Major vs minor major_p = [6.35,2.23,3.48,2.33,4.38,4.09,2.52,5.19,2.39,3.66,2.29,2.88] minor_p = np.roll(chroma_m, -i) mj, _ = stats.pearsonr(rc, major_p) mn, _ = stats.pearsonr(rc, minor_p) if mj > best_corr: best_corr=mj; best_key=note; best_mode="major" if mn > best_corr: best_corr=mn; best_key=note; best_mode="minor" mode_nl = ("majeur" if best_mode=="major" else "mineur") if lang=="nl" else best_mode # ── Energie analyse ─────────────────────────── rms = float(librosa.feature.spectral_centroid(y=y, sr=sr).mean()) bright = "Helder" if centroid > 3000 else ("Warm" if centroid > 1500 else "Donker") # ── Onset detectie — hoeveel syllaben/beats ── onsets = "instrumental": [int(bpm*0.5), int(bpm), int(bpm*2)], "freestyle": [int(bpm*0.5), int(bpm), int(bpm*2)], } bpm_suggestions = BPM_SUGGESTIONS.get(style, [int(bpm)]) bpm_suggestions = [b for b in bpm_suggestions if 55 <= b <= 200] # ── Melodie suggesties op basis van toonsoort ─ CHORD_SUGGESTIONS = { ("C","minor"): ["Cm - Eb - Ab - Bb","Cm - Fm - Gm - Cm","Cm - Ab - Eb - G"], ("C","major"): ["C - G - Am - F","C - F - G - Am","C - Am - F - G"], ("A","minor"): ["Am - F - C - G","Am - Dm - E - Am","Am - G - F - E"], ("D","minor"): ["Dm - Bb - F - C","Dm - Am - Bb - C","Dm - Gm - A - Dm"], ("E","minor"): ["Em - C - G - D","Em - Am - D - G","Em - Bm - C - G"], ("G","major"): ["G - D - Em - C","G - C - D - Em","G - Em - C - D"], ("F","major"): ["F - C - Dm - Am","F - Bb - C - F","F - Am - Bb - C"], ("Bb","minor"): ["Bbm - Gb - Db - Ab","Bbm - Fm - Gb - Ab"], ("Ab","major"): ["Ab - Eb - Fm - Db","Ab - Db - Eb - Ab"], } chords = CHORD_SUGGESTIONS.get((best_key, best_mode), [f"{best_key}m - {best_key}7 - {best_key}m"]) # ── Productie advies per stijl ───────────────── PROD_ADVICE = { "rap": { "nl": [ f"Je flow heeft ~{density:.1f} syllaben/sec — {'snel en dicht' if density>4 else 'rustig en melodisch'}", f"Beste trap/drill BPM: {bpm_suggestions[0]} BPM (half-time feel)", f"Standaard rap BPM: {bpm_suggestions[1] if len(bpm_suggestions)>1 else int(bpm)} BPM", f"808 bas past goed bij toonsoort {best_key} {mode_nl}", "Zet een high-pass bij 100Hz op de vocal voor helderheid", "Compressor op vocal: attack 10ms, release 50ms, ratio 4:1", "Voeg een subtiele reverb toe (pre-delay 20ms) voor diepte", ], "en": [ f"Your flow has ~{density:.1f} syllables/sec — {'fast and dense' if density>4 else 'slow and melodic'}", f"Best trap/drill BPM: {bpm_suggestions[0]} BPM (half-time feel)", f"Standard rap BPM: {bpm_suggestions[1] if len(bpm_suggestions)>1 else int(bpm)} BPM", f"808 bass fits key of {best_key} {best_mode}", "High-pass vocal at 100Hz for clarity", "Vocal compressor: attack 10ms, release 50ms, ratio 4:1", "Add subtle reverb (pre-delay 20ms) for depth", ], }, "singing": { "nl": [ f"Melodie zit rond {best_key} {mode_nl} — bouw hierop verder", f"Melody is around {best_key} {best_mode} — build on this", f"Recommended BPM: {bpm_suggestions[0]} (slow) or {bpm_suggestions[1] if len(bpm_suggestions)>1 else int(bpm)} (standard)", f"Spectral librosa.feature.chroma_cqt(y=y, sr=sr) key_idx= int(np.argmax(chroma.mean(axis=1))) NOTES = ["C","C#","D","Eb","E","F","F#","G","Ab","A","Bb","B"] key = NOTES[key_idx] p95 = _clear_lh(self): self.lh_tracks = [] self.lh_canvas.delete("all") self._write(self.lh_txt, "") self.lh_status.config(text="Cleared — add new tracks") def _refresh_lh(self): if not self.lh_tracks: return # Teken LUFS grafiek self.lh_canvas.update() W = self.lh_canvas.winfo_width() or 800 H = 180; PAD = 40 self.lh_canvas.delete("all") n = len(self.lh_tracks) bar_w = max(20, (W - 2*PAD) // n - 6) lufs_vals = [t["lufs"] for t in self.lh_tracks] lufs_min = min(lufs_vals) - 3 lufs_max = max(lufs_vals) + 3 lufs_range= max(lufs_max - lufs_min, 1) # Target lijnen for target, color, label in [(-14,"#27c45a","Streaming -14"), (-23,"#f0d060","Broadcast -23"), (-27,"#3a8fd9","Film -27")]: if lufs_min <= target <= lufs_max: ty = PAD + H - 2*PAD - int((target-lufs_min)/lufs_range*(H-2*PAD)) self.lh_canvas.create_line(PAD, ty, W-PAD, ty, fill=color, dash=(4,4), width=1) self.lh_canvas.create_text(W-PAD+2, ty, text=label, fill=color, font=("Courier New",7), anchor="w") # Bars COLORS_CYCLE = [TEAL, BLUE, PURPLE, ACCENT2, GREEN, GOLD_LT, ACCENT] for i, track in enumerate(self.lh_tracks): x = PAD + i*(bar_w+6) lufs_y = PAD + H - 2*PAD - int((track["lufs"]-lufs_min)/lufs_range*(H-2*PAD)) col = COLORS_CYCLE[i % len(COLORS_CYCLE)] self.lh_canvas.create_rectangle(x, lufs_y, x+bar_w, H-PAD, fill=col, outline="") self.lh_canvas.create_text(x+bar_w//2, lufs_y-8, text=f"{track['lufs']:.1f}", fill=col, font=("Courier New",7,"bold")) name = track["name"][:10] self.lh_canvas.create_text(x+bar_w//2, H-PAD+8, text=name, fill="#555555", font=("Courier New",7), angle=0) # Tekst tabel out = "── LOUDNESS VERGELIJKING ─────────────────────────────────\n" out += f" {'TRACK':<26} {'LUFS':>7} {'PEAK':>7} {'BPM':>7} {'KEY':>5} {'DR':>6}\n" out += f" {'─'*26} {'─'*7} {'─'*7} {'─'*7} {'─'*5} {'─'*6}\n" for t in self.lh_tracks: out += f" {t['name']:<26} {t['lufs']:>7.1f} {t['peak']:>7.1f} {t['bpm']:>7.0f} {t['key']:>5} {t['dr']:>6.1f}\n" out += f"\n── ADVIES ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n" avg_lufs = sum(t["lufs"] for t in self.lh_tracks) / len(self.lh_tracks) out += f" Gemiddeld LUFS: {avg_lufs:.1f}\n" if avg_lufs > -14: out += " ⚠️ Tracks zijn gemiddeld te luid voor streaming\n" elif avg_lufs < -27: out += " 💡 Tracks zijn erg dynamisch — goed voor film/sync\n" else: out += " ✅ Loudness zit in goede range voor sync\n"
